claims.text: YouTube Data API search.list reports approximate totalResults, not an exact census of matching people, communities or videos.
claims.limitations: Search and relevance sampling cannot establish unique users in a subculture.

claims.text: YouTube Data API channel statistics return subscriberCount rounded to three significant figures.
claims.limitations: Public channel subscriber values are approximate and subscribers may not be active viewers.

claims.text: YouTube Data API channel statistics expose a count of public uploaded videos, not a count of every video ever created.
claims.limitations: Private, unlisted or deleted content cannot be inferred from public counts.

claims.text: YouTube Analytics distinguishes views, engagedViews, watch time, estimated creator revenue, gross revenue and CPM-type metrics.
claims.limitations: The units and reporting basis differ by metric and report; estimated revenues may later be adjusted.

claims.text: YouTube requires creators to classify made-for-kids content using audience-directed factors; general-audience animation is not automatically made for kids.
claims.limitations: Classification depends on content and intent; age-directed legal rules vary by jurisdiction.

claims.text: Made-for-kids content has restrictions including personalized advertising and various social, community and commercial features.
claims.limitations: The exact effects differ for video versus channel settings and may change.

claims.text: YouTube's channel monetization policies require original, authentic content and address repetitive or mass-produced material.
claims.limitations: Content eligibility requires context-sensitive review; a genre alone does not imply monetization.

claims.text: YouTube distinguishes content that may receive full, limited or no advertising revenue under its advertiser-friendly guidelines.
claims.limitations: Per-video suitability can change and is context-dependent.

claims.text: Pew's 2026 survey found 84% of U.S. adults said they ever use YouTube.
claims.limitations: U.S. adults only; ever-use, not MAU, unique global users or monthly video views.

claims.text: DataReportal's Digital 2026 country reports give late-2025 estimated YouTube advertising reach of 85 million in Mexico, 254 million in the United States and 150 million in Brazil.
claims.limitations: These are advertising-planning estimates, not the platforms' monthly active users or deduplicated viewer counts.

claims.text: In a 2025 Pew survey, 92% of U.S. teens ages 13–17 reported ever using YouTube; the subgroup use rates were 94% among boys and 89% among girls.
claims.limitations: A U.S. teen sample distinct from the 2026 U.S. adult survey. These figures do not describe the demographic composition or children's content audiences.

claims.text: In a selected research sample of Patreon accounts with only YouTube as their outside social-platform affiliation, pooled monthly Patreon earnings had a $47 median and $250 mean across 23,435 observations (March 2018, 2021 and 2024).
claims.limitations: This describes off-platform Patreon earnings, not YouTube ads, not total creator income or profit, and not a representative population of all YouTube channels. Creators earning $10 or less on Patreon were excluded and some values were imputed.

claims.text: AIR Media-Tech reports that, in a sample of 297 monetized YouTube channels under 10,000 subscribers, median monthly Studio earnings were USD 88 in the first full month (month 2) and USD 32 in month 6.
claims.limitations: Selected, already-monetized channels only; months began during 2024–2026; publisher is a commercial service, recruitment and independent auditing unspecified. Not representative of all creators or a forecast.

claims.text: Within the same 297-channel cohort, reported median monthly Studio revenue differed by leading viewer country and niche; the smallest reported subgroups had only 10–15 channels.
claims.limitations: The reported niche and country summaries are marginal medians across months 2–6, not a causal or generalizable rate for a creator choosing a country or genre.

claims.text: YouTube describes separate earning features for watch-page ads, Shorts Feed ads, Premium, memberships, Supers, and Shopping. Feature eligibility is distinct from overall YPP entry.
claims.limitations: Not all channels or countries have access to all products; no advertised feature guarantees payment.

claims.text: The YouTube Shopping affiliate program lists Mexico among eligible creator countries. A July 2026 TeamYouTube announcement describes product tagging with Mercado Libre for eligible creators in Mexico and Argentina.
claims.limitations: YPP and program-specific requirements apply; tagging is not a guaranteed commission or a guarantee of brand/merchant availability.

claims.text: YouTube Creator Partnerships supports eligible creators in Mexico, with region-dependent interfaces; the Mexico documentation describes advertiser discovery and offline contact routes.
claims.limitations: Eligibility includes adulthood, YPP ads revenue-sharing eligibility, country and strike restrictions; YouTube does not guarantee a deal.

claims.text: Eligible YPP creators may earn Rubies when viewers use Jewels to send gifts on supported live streams.
claims.limitations: Availability, content/stream eligibility and accepting the Virtual Items module differ from Super Chat; Rubies are not an ordinary 70%-of-Jewels revenue share.

claims.text: YouTube Help lists a MXN-denominated payment threshold of MXN 1,200 and method-selection threshold of MXN 120 for AdSense for YouTube.
claims.limitations: Threshold depends on payment account reporting currency, not residence. Payout is subject to verification, holds and terms.

claims.text: For Mexico payment addresses, YouTube lists electronic funds transfer and wire transfer but not check or Hyperwallet as available payment methods.
claims.limitations: Specific payment account and payment provider requirements still apply; no personal bank details are needed for this research.

claims.text: YouTube said in September 2026 that Shopping affiliate availability was expanding, alongside broader creator brand-partnership tools.
claims.limitations: Some announced functionality is described as testing, coming soon or planned; do not mark a future feature as launched everywhere.

claims.text: YouTube generally finalizes prior-month earnings on the 7th–12th of the next month, checks payment threshold and holds by the 20th, and issues eligible AdSense for YouTube payments between the 21st and 26th.
claims.limitations: Issuance is conditional on threshold, verification, tax and account standing, and is not the same as bank arrival. Specific calendars and holds can shift timing.

claims.text: YouTube says content suitable for a wide audience, including animation appealing to adults and teens, is not automatically classified as made for kids.
claims.limitations: Creators must evaluate the content's actual intended audience and multiple factors; a genre label is not legal advice.

claims.text: YouTube lists personalized advertising, comments, certain live interactions, channel memberships and Shopping or merchandise features among restrictions associated with made-for-kids content or channels.
claims.limitations: Exact restricted features differ between individual video and channel-wide designation and can change.

claims.text: YouTube's channel monetization policy distinguishes original, authentic content from mass-produced, repetitive or minimally reused content.
claims.limitations: Use of an animation or AI tool alone does not decide eligibility; creators must meet the substance and originality requirements.

claims.text: YouTube's 2026 advertiser guideline update describes expanded monetization eligibility for certain public-interest debates and discussions of government actions.
claims.limitations: Context matters; cannot infer that all political content is fully monetized or that any individual creator will qualify.

claims.text: The YouTube Analytics API distinguishes estimatedAdRevenue (estimated net creator income from Google-sold ads), grossRevenue (pre-revenue-share gross ad proceeds), and estimatedRevenue (estimated net revenue from ads and specified non-ad revenue); none is interchangeable with the others.
claims.limitations: Authorized reporting only; estimates subject to adjustments and available metrics depend on query, period and account rights.

claims.text: YouTube distinguishes CPM per thousand ad impressions from playback-based CPM per thousand monetized playbacks; one playback may generate more than one ad impression.
claims.limitations: Both are advertiser-side gross measures and do not equal creator RPM or profit.

claims.text: YouTube Analytics reports.query uses a three-letter currency parameter for supported revenue and ad-performance metrics; the default reported currency is USD, and conversion uses rates that can change daily.
claims.limitations: A converted analytics display currency is not automatically the settlement currency or the creator's tax currency.

claims.text: YouTube publishes authenticated channel analytics examples for daily, video-level, and country-specific revenue measurements; other channels' detailed income and audience demographics are not disclosed through unauthenticated public Data API lookups.
claims.limitations: An authorized channel owner's reports still do not identify a representative population of all YouTube channels.

claims.text: In the GWI data summarized by DataReportal for April 2026, 55.3% of surveyed internet users aged 16+ reported using YouTube in the preceding month; excluding China and Russia from the sample, that share was 70.6%.
claims.limitations: Different geographic denominators; both are survey percentages rather than global unique-user counts or audience composition.

claims.text: YouTube's October 2026 press page reports an average of over 20 million videos uploaded daily and over 200 billion daily Shorts views.
claims.limitations: Upload events and view events; not distinct active creators, Shorts engaged revenue views or unique viewers. Exact press reporting interval not stated.

claims.text: YouTube describes Partner Program review decisions as typically taking about one month; some reviews take longer. It states a 21-day appeal period following a first rejection, a 30-day waiting period before first reapplication, and generally 90 days for later reapplications.
claims.limitations: Typical review interval is not a guaranteed deadline. Appeal and reapplication rules may depend on prior history and policy changes.

claims.text: YouTube says watch hours and views generated by paid advertising campaigns do not count toward YPP qualification thresholds, apart from qualifying organic follow-on views under the documented rules.
claims.limitations: Eligibility counting differs from normal channel analytics and organic follow-on traffic; boosting videos is not a shortcut to YPP.

claims.text: YouTube's advertising monetization requirements allow a creator younger than 18 to have an adult legal guardian manage AdSense for YouTube payments, subject to program and account requirements.
claims.limitations: The option applies to relevant ad revenue eligibility, not automatically to all products requiring an adult creator.

claims.text: YouTube reports that more than 1.7 billion unique viewers worldwide watched World Cup-related videos during the FIFA World Cup 2026 event; over 550 million of them watched on TV devices.
claims.limitations: Measured event-associated audience and subset, not all soccer fans, continuous monthly community membership, or a value derived from view counts.

claims.text: YouTube reports more than 20 billion global views on NFL-related videos in 2025, and over 250% growth in annual related views from 2020 to 2025.
claims.limitations: American football category, not association football; view counts are events, not unique people or representative creator earnings. Longitudinal methods require review.

claims.text: YouTube describes new, casual and regular viewers as separate channel audience segments. Casual viewers have watched in one to five months during the past year, while regular viewers have watched in more than six months.
claims.limitations: Authorized channel audience reporting, not counts of all YouTube users. Private viewing and deleted histories can cause a previously seen viewer to be counted as new.

claims.text: YouTube's channel monthly audience measure is a rolling 28-day estimate of unique viewers, recalculated daily.
claims.limitations: Not the same as calendar-month active users for YouTube as a whole or subscribers to a channel.

claims.text: YouTube counts a registered thumbnail impression when a thumbnail is at least 50% visible for more than one second on eligible YouTube surfaces.
claims.limitations: External links, many notifications, end screens and some product surfaces are excluded from the thumbnail impression denominator.

claims.text: YouTube impression click-through rate counts views generated from registered impressions; total video views can exceed registered impressions because other traffic sources contribute.
claims.limitations: A ratio of all video views to registered impressions is not official impressions CTR.

claims.text: YouTube notes that early thumbnail CTR may be higher among loyal viewers and later fall as impressions reach more people; low impressions can reflect audience saturation or competition.
claims.limitations: CTR and average view duration are descriptive, not an observed probability of viral recommendation or a causal success rule.

claims.text: YouTube Reach reports can separately show search terms, suggesting videos, external websites or apps, playlists and notification traffic.
claims.limitations: Channel-owner reporting, with privacy and product availability limitations; not a complete public record of competitors.

claims.text: YouTube Posts can use polls, quizzes, GIFs, images, music, text and videos, and may appear on channel pages, Home or Subscriptions feeds.
claims.limitations: Supervised accounts and channels set as made for kids cannot use Posts. Visibility does not prove an impression, engagement or monetization.

claims.text: Since August 24, 2026, YouTube's raw public views count playback starts across Shorts, long-form and live video, while YPP earnings and eligibility use other engaged or qualified measures.
claims.limitations: Do not compare raw public views before and after the definition change as identical engagement units.

claims.text: Standard-channel square or vertical uploads up to three minutes made on or after October 15, 2024 generally classify as Shorts; this affects where the video earns advertising revenue.
claims.limitations: Official Artist Channels have a different start date; music and content-rights restrictions can alter availability.

claims.text: Mobile live streaming requires at least 50 subscribers, channel verification, no live-stream restrictions in the preceding 90 days and enabling live features; first activation can take up to 24 hours.
claims.limitations: These are mobile-stream requirements, not a general rule that all webcam or encoder live streams need 50 subscribers.

claims.text: YouTube's current live-streaming guidance requires creators to be at least 16 years old, with additional safeguards when younger teens appear.
claims.limitations: Local laws and child-safety requirements still apply; not a substitute for reviewing terms.

claims.text: On YouTube a podcast is a playlist whose episodes are videos, potentially eligible for YouTube Music listening and podcast-specific discovery.
claims.limitations: A raw MP3 cannot be converted directly into a YouTube podcast; podcast features depend on ownership and policy eligibility.

claims.text: YouTube says URLs in Shorts descriptions and comments are not clickable; a Shorts related-video link can be clickable.
claims.limitations: Available linking and advanced-feature permissions should be verified for the actual channel; mere text URLs do not provide a one-tap purchase path.

claims.text: YouTube Premieres can use live chat and related real-time viewer interactions during a scheduled watch event.
claims.limitations: This is scheduled playback, not the same as a new live-camera broadcast; eligible paid chats and memberships require separate access.

claims.text: Pew Research Center's August 2026 survey found 34% of U.S. adults reported regularly getting news on YouTube; the proportion among YouTube users was 41%.
claims.limitations: Two different survey denominators: U.S. adults and YouTube users. Neither rate is the fraction of all videos that are news or the portion of the YouTube audience that follows political commentary.

claims.text: In a 2025 Pew survey, 57% of U.S. adults who regularly get news on YouTube were men and 42% women; 46% identified with or leaned toward Republicans and 49% toward Democrats.
claims.limitations: The 2025 composition refers only to regular YouTube news consumers, not all viewers, politics-only viewers or prospective purchasers. Other/no party identifications and nonresponse are excluded from these rounded examples.

claims.text: In a 2026 Metricool analysis of 71,177 accounts and 799,718 videos, 9.59% of sampled channels with up to 2,000 subscribers moved up a subscriber-size tier, compared with 16.01% among channels with 2,000–10,000 subscribers.
claims.limitations: 2025–2026 observation period not fully specified; these are within-sample category transitions, not a creator's probability of success or of monetization.

claims.text: Metricool reported that over 61% of the organic video views it observed in its 2026 YouTube dataset came from the Shorts feed, compared with approximately 11% from subscribers and 9% from search.
claims.limitations: Commercially selected source population; the traffic source shares do not represent all YouTube views or unique people. Exact inclusion and date windows are not specified in the public summary.

claims.text: Metricool reported 55% lower estimated ad revenue, 51% fewer ad impressions and 59% fewer monetized playbacks in its analyzed long-form cohort when comparing its 2025 and 2026 samples.
claims.limitations: Within the observed sample; changes may reflect cohort mix, upload behavior, seasonality, view definition, geography and other confounders. Not a claim about platform total ad revenue or typical creator profit.

claims.text: A peer-reviewed study of YouTube channels in Germany, Austria and Switzerland reports an earnings Gini coefficient of 0.89 for its measured or estimated channel earnings distribution.
claims.limitations: The abstract does not resolve the underlying earning-estimation method, country sample frame or inclusion of zero/nonmonetized creators. It is not a global creator earning estimate.

claims.text: In a study of 50 Korean beauty YouTube channels, returning-viewer watch time had the strongest statistical association with monthly revenue among the engagement measures examined.
claims.limitations: Observational panel regression, narrow sample; not proof that increasing returning watch time causes any specified cash payout.

claims.text: A study of 47 Korean beauty YouTube channels found associations between publishing frequency, consistency, format mix and engagement or revenue, with higher Shorts concentration linked to lower sustained watch time.
claims.limitations: A small narrow observational sample does not identify a universal best posting frequency or earnings forecast.

claims.text: A CHI 2025 study analyzed monetized live contribution activity among 1,923 YouTube virtual creators across over one million hours of streamed content.
claims.limitations: Livestream contribution activity is not equal to total VTuber profit or earnings for all channels.

claims.text: YouTube phased out new paid Creator Music track licenses, with August 10, 2026 as the final documented purchase date. Previously applied purchased licenses remain effective until expiry; unused purchased licenses were to be refunded.
claims.limitations: Track-specific terms and historical purchases differ; does not imply licensing of all music is free.

claims.text: YouTube documents Creator Music for eligible U.S. Partner Program creators; eligible long-form revenue-sharing tracks can reduce the standard Watch Page creator share depending on the tracks and other music-rights deductions.
claims.limitations: Not a universal creator income rate, worldwide feature availability or Shorts/live rule.

claims.text: YouTube's Studio Audio Library offers royalty-free production audio, with attribution required for certain Creative Commons tracks under their license terms.
claims.limitations: Rights depend on actual library content and conditions; this does not grant blanket reuse rights outside authorized scope.

claims.text: Content ID claims can lead to geographic blocking, claimant monetization with possible sharing, or viewing-activity tracking.
claims.limitations: Rights holder actions and territorial settings vary; this is not a measured earnings loss.

claims.text: YouTube says monetized Content ID claim disputes can lead to withheld revenue pending resolution; a five-day timing distinction governs when withholding begins.
claims.limitations: Withheld sums are neither confirmed permanent losses nor guaranteed creator revenue; settlement timing and outcomes vary.

claims.text: A Content ID claim does not automatically cause a copyright strike. A valid legal copyright-removal request leads to removal and a strike; YouTube says three strikes within 90 days can lead to channel termination.
claims.limitations: Only describes official enforcement categories and thresholds; not an observed channel-termination frequency or monetary loss.

claims.text: YouTube restricts Creator Music use in videos mainly dedicated to paid brand promotion and excludes YouTube Shopping features for videos using Creator Music revenue-sharing tracks.
claims.limitations: Track-level rules, sponsor-content emphasis and product eligibility differ; this does not measure lost sales.

claims.text: A Google Account allows signed-in YouTube viewing and interaction, but publishing and commenting require a YouTube channel. Personal and Brand channels have different administration possibilities.
claims.limitations: Supervised-account and participation restrictions can affect channel creation and specific features.

claims.text: YouTube provides standard features on eligible channel creation; intermediate features require phone verification; advanced features require phone verification and sufficient channel history or ID/video verification where offered.
claims.limitations: Actual enabled status is account-specific, subject to strikes, daily limits and separate product gates.

claims.text: Advanced identity verification is reserved for the channel's primary owner and is not available through ID or video to every creator; sufficient channel history is an alternative.
claims.limitations: Brand Account management access does not establish authorization to verify; optional identity methods should not be treated as mandatory.

claims.text: YouTube Studio separates uploading a video file from making it publicly visible; videos may be private, unlisted, public, or scheduled.
claims.limitations: Uploads may be disabled for supervised accounts; publication can be restricted by Community Guidelines.

claims.text: Creating a channel or unlocking publishing features does not automatically satisfy YouTube Partner Program eligibility or grant creator payments.
claims.limitations: Different products and countries impose separate eligibility, application review and settlement gates.

claims.text: A 2025 Alitu self-selected survey of 558 independent podcasters reported, among its post-launch respondents, episode-production hour bins of 4% under one hour, 27% at 1–3, 28% at 4–5, 20% at 6–8, 8% at 9–10 and 13% above ten hours.
claims.limitations: Hours measured across a mixed audio/video podcast sample; post-launch subgroup n not given. Not a typical YouTube video production time.

claims.text: The same 2025 sample of post-launch podcasters reported monthly podcast cash spending: 17% no cash outlay, 7% below $10, 40% at $10–$49, 16% at $50–$99, and 20% at $100 or more.
claims.limitations: Self-selected mixed audio/video podcasters, unspecified post-launch respondent n, cash spending excludes value of unpaid labor and potentially existing equipment. Not YouTube costs.

claims.text: In that surveyed post-launch independent podcast group, 85% said their show did not make money; this measures podcasts in the selected survey, not all YouTube channels or all creators.
claims.limitations: Nonrepresentative self-recruited podcast sample; does not establish the YouTube newcomer zero-earning rate.

claims.text: In NeoReach's cross-platform 2025 Creator Earnings Report, 50.71% of over 3,000 surveyed creators reported annual creator earnings below USD 15,000.
claims.limitations: Commercial, mixed-platform sample with undisclosed probability-sampling frame; the collaborating publishers describe the same study, not independent evidence. Does not measure YouTube income distribution or profit.

claims.text: NeoReach reported that approximately 57% of its surveyed full-time creators earned below USD 44,000 annually from content alone.
claims.limitations: Full-time subgroup size and survey weights are unavailable on the public summary; not a YouTube-only or causal statement.

claims.text: Creator Spotlight's December 2025 survey collected 427 self-reported creator responses, of whom 37 (about 8.7%) reported six-figure creator-work earnings for 2025.
claims.limitations: Voluntary responses from engaged newsletter readers across multiple platforms, chiefly North America; cannot establish population-wide or YouTube-newcomer rates.

claims.text: Creator Spotlight described nearly half of its 427 surveyed creator respondents as earning less than USD 500 from creator work in 2025, and reported 92 respondents between USD 1,000 and USD 5,000.
claims.limitations: Nearly half is qualitative, not an exact count or percentage; respondents include non-YouTube platforms and are not a representative YouTube cohort.

claims.text: Ofcom's December 2025 Online Nation public briefing reports YouTube use by 94% of UK adults, on its UK online-audience measurement basis.
claims.limitations: Use/reach from regulator briefing is not a worldwide monthly audience size. Exact time window and weighting must be taken from the full methodology.

claims.text: Ofcom's 2025 Online Nation briefing reports 51 minutes per day on YouTube, excluding television-set viewing.
claims.limitations: Time-per-user versus time-per-all-adults denominator in short briefing is not fully specified; it cannot be summed with Barb in-home viewing minutes.

claims.text: Ofcom's July 2026 Media Nations briefing says UK per-person daily YouTube viewing on TV sets increased from 9 minutes in 2022 to 19 minutes in 2025; total in-home connected-device viewing was 33 versus 41 minutes per person.
claims.limitations: Barb in-home measures exclude out-of-home/mobile-network viewing; all-device figures already include TV, so amounts may not be added.

claims.text: Ofcom reports weekly YouTube reach among UK people aged 75 and over of 28% in 2022 and 33% in 2025.
claims.limitations: These are prevalence rates within the 75+ age group, not YouTube audience-composition shares or inferred individual identities.

claims.text: Reuters Institute's 2026 Digital News Report describes YouTube use for any purpose by 69% of respondents across its surveyed markets and for news by 34%; these are separate questions and measurement windows.
claims.limitations: 48-market online survey averages do not represent all world residents. News use is not a share of watch time, ads or YouTube videos.

claims.text: YouTube's multi-language audio feature allows creators with supported advanced-feature access to upload secondary audio tracks for eligible videos and Shorts; long-form videos can also receive localized thumbnail artwork.
claims.limitations: Creator-supplied recordings, not automatic audio; eligibility and thumbnail support differ by content format and specific channel.

claims.text: YouTube documents that automatic dubbing can fail eligibility for videos over 120 minutes, without spoken content, in unsupported source languages, with fast speech or copyright claims; generated dubs may contain language errors.
claims.limitations: Not every translation pair or channel is supported, and operational features may change.

claims.text: YouTube reported in September 2025 that creators uploading multi-language audio tracks received over 25% of their video watch time from non-primary-language views, in the product sample as of July 2025.
claims.limitations: Selected creators only; denominator is watch minutes, not distinct viewers or causally additional views. No new channel income or costs established.

claims.text: YouTube's May 2026 auto-dubbing explanation described support across 27 languages at that time, eight with Expressive Speech.
claims.limitations: Dated rollout snapshot, not proof every current channel has every language or translation pair.

claims.text: YouTube lets viewers set preferred audio, title and description languages separately from their interface and location settings, and choose available audio tracks per video.
claims.limitations: Preferred language is not reliable evidence of an individual's nationality, ethnicity, age or other demographic characteristics.

claims.text: On August 24, 2026, YouTube began counting public video views from the first playback frame across Shorts, long-form, podcasts and live, including autoplay and hover playback.
claims.limitations: Public start-event counts are not unique people or automatically eligible program watch activity. Pre/post raw counts differ in definition.

claims.text: YouTube distinguishes public playback starts from engaged views, which reflect an explicit click/tap or watching beyond initial seconds. Passive thumbnail displays without started playback remain impressions.
claims.limitations: Engaged activity is still subject to separate product and qualification rules; exact thresholds may differ by context.

claims.text: YouTube states that its August 2026 public-view definition change did not directly alter recommendation rules, key engaged-view-based analytics or Partner Program qualification requirements.
claims.limitations: Says no change by this counting policy, not evidence that channel monetization or view distributions stayed constant for every creator.

claims.text: Google's October 15, 2026 Data API quota guidance lists a default 100 daily search.list call allowance at one unit per call, a separate 100 videos.insert call allowance, and 10,000 daily units for other endpoints.
claims.limitations: Defaults, not confirmed quotas for any specific project. Each page request consumes its method bucket; daily reset is Pacific Time.

claims.text: YouTube Data API search.list accepts at most 50 result items per call and defines pageInfo.totalResults as an approximate result count capped at 1,000,000; pagination must use nextPageToken.
claims.limitations: Actual returned page size may be lower. This cannot establish population size, completeness of a topic corpus or count of distinct creators.

claims.text: Google documents one-unit calls to videos.list and channels.list within the shared other-endpoint quota; videos.list permits metadata retrieval of up to 50 specified video IDs per call.
claims.limitations: This describes public resource access, not exhaustive enumeration, a consented creator cohort or authority to collect nonpublic information.

claims.text: YouTube reported more than 250 million cumulative or period views globally for videos related to handmade jewelry with DIY in the title (2025).
claims.limitations: Only the platform-defined content/title subset and reporting window, not distinct viewers, active creators, channel profitability or a representative niche market.

claims.text: YouTube reported more than 300 million cumulative or period views globally for videos related to polymer clay with miniature in the title (2025).
claims.limitations: Only the platform-defined content/title subset and reporting window, not distinct viewers, active creators, channel profitability or a representative niche market.

claims.text: YouTube reported more than 100 million cumulative or period views globally for videos with draw with me or #drawwithme in their title (2025).
claims.limitations: Only the platform-defined content/title subset and reporting window, not distinct viewers, active creators, channel profitability or a representative niche market.

claims.text: YouTube reported more than 100 million cumulative or period views globally for videos with paint with me or #paintwithme in their title (2025).
claims.limitations: Only the platform-defined content/title subset and reporting window, not distinct viewers, active creators, channel profitability or a representative niche market.

claims.text: YouTube reported more than 250 million cumulative or period views globally for videos with bento box or #bentobox in their titles (2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30).
claims.limitations: Only the platform-defined content/title subset and reporting window, not distinct viewers, active creators, channel profitability or a representative niche market.

claims.text: YouTube reported more than 620 million cumulative or period views globally for videos with buldak and ramen in their titles (2025-01-01 to 2025-10-10).
claims.limitations: Only the platform-defined content/title subset and reporting window, not distinct viewers, active creators, channel profitability or a representative niche market.

claims.text: YouTube reported more than 100 million cumulative or period views globally for videos related to sewing machines with beginner in their titles (2025).
claims.limitations: Only the platform-defined content/title subset and reporting window, not distinct viewers, active creators, channel profitability or a representative niche market.

claims.text: YouTube reported more than 16,000 million cumulative or period views globally for a single Baby Shark Dance video, cumulative through June 2025 (through 2025-06).
claims.limitations: Single music video's cumulative plays are not the child-viewer population. Never infer a user's age from viewing.

claims.text: On August 10, 2026 YouTube announced that from February 1, 2027 new YPP ads/Premium applicants will require 8,000 qualified public watch hours in 365 days or 20 million qualified Shorts views in 90 days, replacing current 4,000 or 10 million thresholds.
claims.limitations: Announced future rule, not yet operative October 2026. Blog does not expressly restate 2027 subscriber threshold, so it is unknown; channel approval still needed.

claims.text: YouTube says the new 2027 YPP ads/Premium entry requirements will not affect creators already in the Partner Program.
claims.limitations: Does not waive ongoing policy, activity, contract or product-specific qualification rules.

claims.text: From February 1, 2027, Shorts revenue sharing will depend on 10 million qualified Shorts views in the previous 90 days, even for current YPP creators; creators below the threshold remain YPP members and can continue eligible long-form earning while Shorts sharing is paused.
claims.limitations: Product-specific rolling gate; not equivalent to the 20 million qualified Shorts views required to join YPP ads/Premium as a new 2027 applicant.

claims.text: YouTube announced subscription pools from Premium (30%) and Premium Lite (60%) net subscription revenue and downstream creator shares of 55% for long-form and 45% for Shorts, allocated using member watch time and views.
claims.limitations: Percentages operate on specific net bases, not full retail subscription prices or guaranteed per-view payouts. Actual creator receipts not reported.

claims.text: YouTube Help says YPP creators should accept updated monetization terms by January 31, 2027, for terms effective February 1, 2027, to continue full monetization.
claims.limitations: General guidance; no inference about a particular account's acceptance status or exact outcome of missing deadline.

claims.text: YouTube's August 2026 announcement says fan-funding and Shopping YPP entry thresholds will remain unchanged in the February 2027 update.
claims.limitations: Other product, regional, age, channel and review restrictions still apply; early access is not automatic advertising revenue sharing.

claims.text: YouTube's October 2026 advertiser-policy update clarifies that certain civic and public-interest proceedings and debates on ongoing government action may qualify to earn advertising revenue.
claims.limitations: Official source gives a change month, not a specific effective day. Content context and other advertiser policies still govern decisions; no observed earnings uplift.

claims.text: YouTube's September 2026 guidance expands advertising eligibility for gaming/scripted depictions of recreational drugs and non-glorifying educational or PSA discussion of trafficking.
claims.limitations: Contextual product suitability is not permission to promote dangerous or prohibited conduct. Full advertisement eligibility may depend on other content features.

claims.text: YouTube's September 2026 advertiser-suitability guidance distinguishes potentially ad-eligible graphic game violence in seconds 8–15 from ineligible graphic game violence during the first seven seconds.
claims.limitations: Video, thumbnails, context, content emphasis and other policy gates can change individual ad suitability; no genre-wide RPM estimate.

claims.text: YouTube's August 2026 advertiser update clarifies eligibility for depictions of death in educational, documentary and journalistic contexts.
claims.limitations: No blanket permission for violent or graphic footage; review must consider the full content and title/thumbnail context.

claims.text: YouTube's January 2026 advertiser-policy revisions allow certain non-graphic, dramatized depictions of controversial issues to earn ads, subject to specific exceptions.
claims.limitations: Does not prove a particular political or controversial video will earn ads; ads eligibility and channel approval are separate.

claims.text: Google documents that changing the primary owner of a Brand Account requires the initiating owner to have held ownership for at least seven days and the incoming owner/manager to have held an eligible role for at least seven days.
claims.limitations: This is a role-tenure rule, not a guarantee that all transfers complete in exactly seven days.

claims.text: YouTube Studio channel permissions support roles for collaborators but the Studio Owner role cannot directly transfer Brand Account primary ownership; limited editor/viewer roles restrict access to revenue data.
claims.limitations: Role capability varies by settings, surface, and channel; not an independent right to sell or assign channel assets.

claims.text: YouTube warns that moving a channel between Brand Accounts can permanently delete the existing target channel and its content, and may lose source-side account history/settings.
claims.limitations: Specific losses depend on source and destination; general help does not confirm preservation of all YPP rights, badges, histories or earnings.

claims.text: YouTube permits owners to download eligible uploaded videos through Studio and use Google Takeout; Studio downloads may be limited by file resolution, strikes, audio rights and daily download frequency.
claims.limitations: Downloaded video files do not themselves represent portable subscribers, production projects, paid licenses, monetization approval or customer relationships.

claims.text: YouTube's termination help describes channel appeals within one year and up to two appeals during that period, while terminated creators lose normal YouTube content downloads and may retain access to Google data.
claims.limitations: Legal copyright counter-notices are separate; termination appeal success and timing are unknown, and limits can vary by channel.

claims.text: In CreatorIQ and Influencers.club's 2026 survey of 5,095 creators from 100 regions, 67% of respondents reported annual creator income under USD 10,000 and 62% said content creation was not their primary income source.
claims.limitations: Mixed-platform commercial survey, May 29–June 29, 2026; recruitment and item nonresponse rates not established. Counts do not establish representative YouTube newcomer earnings or probability-based margins of error.

claims.text: In a historical end-of-2019 sample of 153,770 YouTube channels with at least 100,000 subscribers, Rieder and colleagues report that 75.37% had marketplace URLs in fewer than 20% of their videos and 94% had crowdfunding URLs in fewer than 20%.
claims.limitations: Sample focuses on highly subscribed channels and links in descriptions, not actual purchases or earnings; observations are historical and cannot represent all 2026 YouTube channels or first-time creators.

claims.text: Twitch streamer monetization, TikTok Creator Rewards and Vimeo OTT each describe different eligibility and money flows: livestream community support and advertising, eligible short-video performance rewards, and direct paid video-content distribution respectively.
claims.limitations: This is a comparison of product mechanisms documented by their operators, not a representative comparison of earnings, demand, creator populations, viewer populations, or return per hour.

claims.text: YouTube requires all monetizing YPP creators to submit U.S. tax information. For a non-U.S. payee with accepted tax information, applicable U.S. withholding concerns earnings attributable to U.S. viewers and can vary with residence, tax-treaty eligibility and payee status.
claims.limitations: Google's documentation defines platform withholding, not any creator's final total tax liability. No treaty entitlement, personal rate, income or tax filing details are inferred.

claims.text: YouTube's official help warns that missing required tax information can cause withholding up to 24% of worldwide earnings for individual accounts, while specified non-U.S. business accounts can face a different maximum withholding base on U.S. earnings.
claims.limitations: These are conditional Google payment deductions and document-status rules, not a universal tax rate or final creator net profit; actual rates vary by residency, account type and recognized documentation.

claims.text: In The Influencer Marketing Factory's January 2026 survey of 1,000 U.S. creators aged 18–65, 37% of respondents reported typically spending 5–10 hours per week creating content and 8.4% reported 20–40 hours.
claims.limitations: Cross-platform vendor survey with unverified sampling frame, response probabilities, and per-question respondent count; does not establish YouTube-only creator hours, median production effort, full-time employment, costs or profit.

claims.text: YouTube requires creators to declare brand-influenced paid or in-kind consideration through Studio; the paid-promotion disclosure does not by itself settle distinct local legal obligations.
claims.limitations: Jurisdiction, advertiser or endorsement circumstance and the content surface can require additional prominent disclosures; no individual legal determination.

claims.text: In September 2026 TeamYouTube announced updated viewer labels, creator-set age and geographic limits for branded content and a staged automated detection and labeling rollout.
claims.limitations: A rollout announcement does not establish universal account-level feature availability, successful enforcement, or immunity from platform or legal review.

claims.text: FTC guidance for U.S.-consumer-relevant endorsements distinguishes money and in-kind material connections, warns that a platform label alone may not suffice, and says a video description alone is inadequate to disclose an endorsement made in the video.
claims.limitations: FTC staff guidance is context-specific and not a legal safe harbor; the FTC's U.S. consumer scope must not be generalized as worldwide law.

claims.text: YouTube describes possible continued advertising monetization on policy-compliant branded videos by eligible YPP channels, but also states that branded-content videos are removed from YouTube Kids.
claims.limitations: Ad revenue still depends on eligibility, advertiser suitability and ad demand; removal from the Kids app is not a claim that the entire video is deleted from YouTube.

claims.text: TeamYouTube's October 21, 2026 announcement describes temporary account-action restrictions when unauthorized activity is suspected, while existing videos remain viewable and monetization status is not changed by the security pause.
claims.limitations: The announced security review is typically within 24 hours, not a fixed recovery deadline; triggering frequency, false positives, and rollout coverage are unknown.

claims.text: YouTube's hacked-channel Help requires recovering and securing the associated Google Account before cleaning up unauthorized channel changes, and currently notes a nine-month window for potential hijacking-support access.
claims.limitations: Nine months concerns support/data retention, not a guaranteed appeal or outcome; authentication choices and individual cases vary.

claims.text: YouTube documents live-chat restricted participation, blocked words, moderator actions, slow mode, held messages, and hiding users; these controls do not by themselves establish harassment prevalence or complete safety.
claims.limitations: Actual moderation results, community behavior, role permissions and the prevalence of harmful content are unmeasured.

claims.text: YouTube prohibits specified harassment behaviors including some threats, disclosure of non-public personal information, and coordinated abuse, and separately offers privacy complaint procedures for certain unauthorized or realistic synthetic likeness content.
claims.limitations: Not every harmful interaction necessarily violates published platform rules or produces a successful removal; no individual victims or reports are profiled.

claims.text: YouTube owner-facing unique-viewer estimates account for signed-in and signed-out viewers and people watching across devices, with a reporting period of up to 90 days; Shorts use engaged views in estimation.
claims.limitations: Owner-facing channel and video estimates do not identify individual persons, logged-out share or total global platform users.

claims.text: YouTube Studio's monthly audience is a channel-specific estimated unique-person audience measured over a rolling past 28 days and recalculated daily, not an exact calendar-month worldwide user count.
claims.limitations: Period and population differ from owner unique viewers, co-viewing and public channel statistics.

claims.text: YouTube's public Data API provides channel view events, rounded subscribers and public upload counts; Analytics reporting requires authorized channel/content-owner access and does not offer public competitor unique-person data.
claims.limitations: Those public counts describe channel objects and activity, not global unique viewers, independent people or a survey-weighted population.

claims.text: In Pew Research Center's 2026 U.S. adult survey, 77% of adults with high school or less education, 87% with some college, and 90% of college graduates reported ever using YouTube.
claims.limitations: These are YouTube usage rates within education groups, not the educational composition of YouTube users. Survey-wide sample size and margin of error do not describe each subgroup's uncertainty.

claims.text: Pew's 2026 U.S. adult survey reported YouTube ever-use of 77% among household incomes below USD 30,000, 84% at USD 30,000–69,999, 86% at USD 70,000–99,999, and 90% at USD 100,000 or more.
claims.limitations: Rates within self-reported U.S. household-income groups, not YouTube audience income composition, total people or any creator profitability. Subgroup n and subgroup sampling errors not established.

claims.text: Pew's 2026 U.S. adult survey reported YouTube ever-use among 87% of urban, 86% of suburban and 78% of rural respondents.
claims.limitations: Self-reported use within Pew's community groups; not a rural or urban active-viewer population, niche preference or causal effect. Per-group uncertainty remains unknown.

claims.text: YouTube Studio's owner Reach report classifies traffic from browse features, suggested videos, Shorts, search, notifications, playlists, external referrals and direct-or-unknown sources, among other categories.
claims.limitations: Actual traffic counts require channel access and source definitions may include signed-out or unidentified sources; a category does not establish algorithmic causes or creator income.

claims.text: YouTube's Reach documentation describes external links and embeds separately from direct or unknown sources, which can include bookmarks, signed-out viewers and unidentified apps.
claims.limitations: An observed external or direct/unknown event does not prove retained audience ownership, permission to export user identifiers, or income independence.

claims.text: Omdia's January 2026 research release estimates 29 billion YouTube videos by December 2025 and reports that the top 1% of observed videos accounted for 91% of viewing time.
claims.limitations: Commercial analyst summary without sufficient public raw sampling design. Video stock and time concentration differ from unique channels, people, creators, income, or current 2026 audience.

claims.text: Omdia's January 2026 press summary reported 33% of viewing time for music, 10% for news, 5% for video podcasts, 46% as professionally filmed content, and Shorts above 90% of new uploads.
claims.limitations: Music, news, podcast and production-style categories may overlap. Different denominators: share of time versus share of newly uploaded videos. No platform-native measurement codebook or earnings model.

claims.text: In a platform-commissioned April 2026 U.S. online survey of 496 people aged 14–29, 69% reported watching content they considered niche, and 71% reported watching videos explaining stories within a fandom or community.
claims.limitations: Selected self-reported U.S. online respondents ages 14–29, including minors. Neither percentage is a census of actual YouTube viewers or a niche audience size. The behaviors and interests can overlap.

claims.text: In a separate NRG/YouTube 2026 U.S. online respondent group aged 14–44 (n=939), 73% agreed YouTube was the best place to explore personal interests deeply and 72% agreed it helped maintain interest after discovery.
claims.limitations: Self-reported attitudinal agreement; 939 is the reported study sample, not observed platform behavior, a view-count denominator, earnings evidence or a representative world-wide estimate.

claims.text: YouTube's April 2025 Culture & Trends post reports more than 200 million global views of videos related to video essays during calendar 2024.
claims.limitations: Publisher-described topical classification, not 2026 video-essay viewing, unique fans, verified essayists or creator revenue.

claims.text: YouTube's June 2026 upcycling article reports more than 80,000 global 2025 uploads bearing upcycle or upcycling in their titles.
claims.limitations: Title-phrase matched upload objects; misses videos without those words and cannot establish creator count, watch time, owner profit or total craft content supply.

claims.text: YouTube's April 2026 learning article reports more than 79 million views on NASA's primary Artemis II mission stream between April 1 and April 13, 2026.
claims.limitations: One event stream, not all science explainers, original viewers, cumulative science-learning hours, child audiences or creator income.

claims.text: AIR Media-Tech reports a USD 2.30 median RPM per 1,000 views among 300 selected monetized client channels, using 3,595 observed channel-months from May 2025 to May 2026.
claims.limitations: Not a probability sample of YouTube creators; client channels had 10,000 to 50 million subscribers and only monetized months. RPM is after platform's revenue allocation but not creator profit, hourly income or pay including zero-earning entrants.

claims.text: In AIR's 300-channel monetized sample, publisher-reported median RPMs were USD 10.22 for Education & Science, USD 2.05 for Gaming, and USD 0.33 for Kids & Teens; their P25/P75 spreads differ considerably.
claims.limitations: Selected AIR affiliates with uneven small niche samples and unknown per-niche sample counts; not defensible as platform-wide RPM floors or niche rankings, and no cost, retention or margin outcomes shown.

claims.text: AIR's livestream report covers 404 channels over 3,893 performance channel-months, but its monetized live revenue cohort consists of 127 streaming channels and 1,287 monetized streaming channel-months; that subsample had a reported median of 45 views per livestream.
claims.limitations: Streaming months are repeated observations, not 1,287 independent channels; nonmonetized, new and unrepresented streamer earnings not measured. Livestream view counts use historical 2025-early-2026 view definitions.

claims.text: YouTube permits mid-roll ad slots for eligible monetized watch-page videos at least eight minutes long, with manual and automated placement; a slot does not promise an ad impression or revenue.
claims.limitations: Eligibility, source permissions, device, rights and account status govern individual results; no creator earnings inferred.

claims.text: YouTube classifies qualifying square or vertical uploads up to three minutes as Shorts from October 15, 2024 for ordinary channels and December 8, 2025 for official artist channels; older qualifying uploads may retain watch-page treatment.
claims.limitations: Eligibility, source permissions, device, rights and account status govern individual results; no creator earnings inferred.

claims.text: YouTube Live, Premieres, Clips and podcast-designated playlists are different surfaces: a Premiere becomes a regular upload afterwards, a clip references an original video, and a podcast episode is a video belonging to a designated podcast playlist.
claims.limitations: Eligibility, source permissions, device, rights and account status govern individual results; no creator earnings inferred.

claims.text: YouTube says it can archive livestreams under twelve hours, recommends a local recording, and warns that longer streams might not be captured; an archive's replay demand is not guaranteed.
claims.limitations: Eligibility, source permissions, device, rights and account status govern individual results; no creator earnings inferred.

claims.text: Official YouTube Help pages disagree about current treatment of claimed Shorts longer than one minute: the English overview still describes automatic blocking, while another localized Help page describes a September 24, 2026 relaxation for new uploads.
claims.limitations: Conflicting locale Help documents: no universal claim-blocking outcome or new monetization eligibility is inferred.

claims.text: Barb reports that in Q2 2025, among people aged 16+ in its UK in-home Wi-Fi YouTube viewing measurement, TV sets accounted for 43% of viewing and smartphones for 32%.
claims.limitations: Shares of measured viewing by device, not shares of unique viewers or population; UK in-home Wi-Fi measurement excludes mobile network and out-of-home use.

claims.text: Barb reports a TV-set share of 53% of in-home Wi-Fi YouTube viewing for children aged 4–15 in Q2 2025, while its separate TV-set ACR-based report of 200 selected channels explicitly excludes Shorts, live streaming, music/karaoke and other categories.
claims.limitations: Child device share is aggregate service-level viewing, not identification of individual minors. The 200-channel ACR sample cannot represent all YouTube, and its exclusions must not be incorrectly applied to the service-wide device shares.

claims.text: YouTube explicitly distinguishes child-directed mixed audiences from general-family animation: being family-friendly or including cartoons does not automatically make content intended for children.
claims.limitations: Content classification, legal age definitions and survey populations are conditional on the specific source, country and period; no individual child or creator income inferred.

claims.text: YouTube's made-for-kids designation removes personalized advertising and disables or restricts comments, notification features, live chat and several fan-funding or commerce interactions for affected videos.
claims.limitations: Content classification, legal age definitions and survey populations are conditional on the specific source, country and period; no individual child or creator income inferred.

claims.text: YouTube 18+ age-restricted content is unavailable to signed-out or underage viewers and may have limited ads; it is a different classification from made-for-kids or general-audience animation.
claims.limitations: Content classification, legal age definitions and survey populations are conditional on the specific source, country and period; no individual child or creator income inferred.

claims.text: Ofcom reported that 96% of UK children aged 8–14 in its 2025 online measurement used YouTube, while the sample population differs from adult survey frames and from 4–15-year-old in-home Barb viewing measures.
claims.limitations: Content classification, legal age definitions and survey populations are conditional on the specific source, country and period; no individual child or creator income inferred.

claims.text: YouTube Culture & Trends reported more than 450,000 global video uploads in January–June 2026 with 'morning routine' or 'morningroutine' in their titles.
claims.limitations: Count of uploaded videos meeting a title-filter rule, not all lifestyle videos, independent channels, unique viewers, video views or audience demand.

claims.text: YouTube reported more than 5.5 billion U.S. learning and how-to content views in June 2025; the broad category does not identify science, software or financial tutorial segments.
claims.limitations: Publisher-defined broad topic and monthly view events from June 2025, before 2026 play-start revision; not unique people, tutorial creators, earnings or a time series.

claims.text: YouTube Studio offers owner-only post impressions and top-post engagement metrics, but these counters do not directly identify distinct people who subsequently became recurring video viewers.
claims.limitations: Per-post impression, vote and likes metrics differ in units and do not prove an incremental retention effect or a cross-surface joined attribution funnel.

claims.text: YouTube distinguishes creator Posts from subscriber-generated discussions inside Communities; subscriber participation in a Community can require a creator-selected minimum subscription period.
claims.limitations: Community feature availability and moderation vary; participation counts are not recurring video viewers.

claims.text: YouTube defines casual viewers as watching at least monthly for one to five months of the past year and regular viewers as watching at least monthly for more than six months; these are owner-channel viewing classifications, not measured effects of any Post.
claims.limitations: The owner's rolling 28-day monthly audience and 12-month viewer watch history use different windows; new viewers may include those with cleared histories or a year of inactivity.

claims.text: YouTube Studio differentiates total members who retain perk access from active paid subscribers, gained/canceled/lost members and membership transactions, which can be new sign-ups or recurring charges.
claims.limitations: A membership transaction count is not unique paying humans or a cohort retention probability; monthly billing periods can be 28, 30 or 31 days. Individual channel financial outcomes are not published.

claims.text: YouTube Promote distinguishes ad-attributed subscribers and watch hours, which do not count toward YPP eligibility, from later organic Follow-on Views after exposure to promotion, which can contribute to eligible YPP activity under product rules.
claims.limitations: Promotion metrics are not a verified causal incremental lift or channel-specific profitability outcome; other YPP qualification requirements still apply.

claims.text: Promote's Studio dashboard reports actual ad spend, impressions, paid views, subscribed-after-ad attribution and website clicks; the product defines promotion subscribers by video watch of at least 10 seconds or ad click with subscription within three days.
claims.limitations: Attributed subscriber count does not equal an independently randomized effect, future loyalty or a YPP-qualifying organic subscriber.

claims.text: Google Ads defines billed TrueView video views differently: in-stream requires 30 seconds, video end if shorter or an interaction; in-feed may count a clicked thumbnail or at least 10 seconds autoplay; Shorts requires 10 seconds, video end if shorter or CTA click.
claims.limitations: Billable video ad TrueView views are not identical to public YouTube playback starts, unique people, or organic engaged-view standards; no universal CPV is supported.

claims.text: YouTube Promotions can undergo advertising-policy review for approximately one or two days, be disapproved or serve slowly under restrictive targeting, and Google Ads reports paid and organic video performance under distinct reporting views.
claims.limitations: Review durations are guidance, not guaranteed. No cross-channel average promotion spend, attributable incremental revenue or break-even return is measured.

claims.text: In its September 23, 2026 blog announcement, YouTube said more than 300 million users engage with posts on an average day.
claims.limitations: Platform-reported average daily engaged users with no independent method, regional breakdown, account deduplication definition, creator-post impressions, per-channel retention or earnings. Not a public verified global unique monthly people count.

claims.text: YouTube said microdramas surpassed 6.5 billion video views in the first half of 2026, while microdrama watch time grew by over 50% and microdrama TV views by over 90% year-over-year.
claims.limitations: Publisher-defined microdrama genre and historical view definition; publisher does not disclose exact matching set, baseline counts, unique viewers, channel count or creator net profit. Two relative changes use separate metrics.

claims.text: YouTube's October 12, 2026 Creative Capital EU27 consultation reported responses from more than 20,000 creators; in selected question results, 63% cited little or no support engaging government, 64% said greater traditional-industry recognition would help, and 60% reported insufficient specialized training/workforce support.
claims.limitations: Platform-sponsored consultation, not a population-probability survey. Per-question respondent counts, recruitment frame, response probabilities, subgroup composition and weighting were not established from the public blog.

claims.text: YouTube's EU27 creator consultation reports 65% lacking public grant access, a distinct 65% of professional creators without studio-space access, 83% considering recommendation algorithms vital for growth and revenue, and 71% saying diminished recommendation visibility would endanger their livelihood.
claims.limitations: Different question bases and potentially different subsets; 65% professional-creator studio figure must not be assigned to the entire 20,000+ sample. These are self-reported barriers and perceptions, not actual causal income loss.

claims.text: YouTube's EU consultation announcement states that over 70% of watch time for EU27-channel content originated outside the EU27 and cites a separate Oxford Economics 2025 impact estimate of more than EUR 8.4 billion in EU GDP and 220,000 full-time-equivalent supported jobs.
claims.limitations: Cross-border watch-time fraction differs from unique international viewers; Oxford GDP and FTE are modeled macroeconomic impacts, not earned creator payouts, unique creators or consultation respondent employment.

claims.text: YouTube's current Collaborations Help allows inviting up to ten creators to a long-form video, Short, or archived livestream, with collaborators' channel labels after acceptance and generated YouTube revenue accruing to the channel that uploaded the video, not split automatically.
claims.limitations: Invitation is not proof of acceptance; revenue distribution is the platform's native allocation, not a claim about any separate creator contract or actual revenue amount.

claims.text: YouTube says collaboration-video recommendations may reach both the uploader's and collaborators' audiences, but it does not guarantee immediate changes in search, impressions or recommendations.
claims.limitations: No observed cross-channel incremental reach, subscription gain, watch-hour change, collaboration fee, or newcomer profitability was measured.

claims.text: A historical YouTube product rollout described a five-collaborator limit; the Help page retrieved in October 2026 specifies a ten-collaborator limit, illustrating a changed product specification rather than a controlled growth experiment.
claims.limitations: Exact rollout availability by account, geographical market and intermediate revision dates are unknown. Historical limits must not be presented as current.

claims.text: YouTube's April 2026 NRG U.S. online sample of 496 people aged 14–29 reported perceptions that YouTube creators (77%) and memes (78%) are widely known. These are survey perceptions, not measured video view or community-unique-person populations.
claims.limitations: Commissioned, nonprobability sampling design not established publicly; question-level respondent counts and variance not independently verified. Do not treat source categories as nonoverlapping.

claims.text: YouTube's April 2026 NRG U.S. online sample of 939 people aged 14–44 reported 63% agreement that a favored person's success felt like their own and 60% pride in having contributed to that success.
claims.limitations: Platform-commissioned attitudinal survey, not validated donation, fandom membership, direct creator earnings, or causal influence of fans on creator success.

claims.text: YouTube's December 2025 cultural roundup described fan-made adaptations of television and music phenomena and creator-originated Roblox trends as illustrative cases of remix and community co-creation.
claims.limitations: Editorially selected examples, not a dated network diffusion panel or representative estimate of how frequently memes cross channels.

claims.text: YouTube's January 2024 learning-to-code guide gives examples of beginner programming classes, website development and game scripting, providing illustrative categories but no audited counts of software learners or programming-channel earnings.
claims.limitations: Editor-selected beginner examples cannot establish channel population, completion, tutorial demand or revenue.

claims.text: YouTube reports more than 250 million global views during January–June 2026 of videos with 'desk setup' or '#desksetup' in their titles, a title-query video-view total rather than unique people or creator sales.
claims.limitations: The query includes lifestyle/workspace topics and gaming, not all technical education, programming or all desk setup videos; no verified creator costs or unique viewers.

claims.text: YouTube's April 2026 learning announcement cites more than 5.5 billion U.S. learning/how-to video views in June 2025, but does not break out software tutorials or programming as a separately quantified subset.
claims.limitations: Publisher-defined learning/how-to genre and a single U.S. month; no unique people, niche share, creator compensation or causal teaching outcome.

claims.text: Creative Commons recommends identification of title, author/licensor, source and license when reusing CC-licensed works; simply providing a link to any public webpage is not proof the work is CC-licensed or that a third-party image or dataset can be republished.
claims.limitations: CC0 and public-domain works have different rules; applicable licenses, fair-use exceptions and local copyright law require individual review. This does not grant permission to copy other publishers' assets.

claims.text: An October 2024 YouTube culture report highlighted independently produced animation, fan-created edits and a commissioned U.S. 14–24 online survey where 22% of 350 respondents reported awareness of The Amazing Digital Circus.
claims.limitations: Series-specific awareness in one May 2024 U.S. online youth survey is not a whole animation population, audience growth series or proof of creator profits.

claims.text: A March 2025 YouTube editorial trend report described animation memes as replicable short character-and-audio formats and highlighted fan-created edits around independently produced animated series.
claims.limitations: Curated editorial observation, not an exhaustive or probability-sampled list, quantified audience or platform-wide growth rate.

claims.text: Separate Google/SmithGeiger animation-fan online samples fielded in April 2025 reported 63% weekly independent animation viewing among 358 U.S. fans ages 14–24 and 84% weekly animation-meme viewing among 379 Mexican fans ages 14–24, each under different questions.
claims.limitations: Different countries, question wording, recruitment, fandom framing and sample populations prevent subtracting percentages to infer country gaps, growth or universal prevalence.

claims.text: On August 28, 2023, YouTube reported over six billion views during 2023 to date of videos whose titles contained variations of GRWM, without disclosing an exhaustive title-pattern query.
claims.limitations: Part-year view events, not people, full-year total, constant search definition or earnings.

claims.text: YouTube reports over 25 million 2024 views on titles containing prom and GRWM, more than one billion 2025-to-October-5 views on titles containing halloween and makeup, and more than 100 million 2025 views on sewing-machine-related titles also containing beginner.
claims.limitations: Different searches and event periods can overlap; these are first-party global viewing aggregates, not unique viewers, category market sizes or a comparable annual trend.

claims.text: YouTube reports more than 450,000 global uploads from January to June 2026 with morning routine or morningroutine in the title; this is an upload-object count, not a video-view count.
claims.limitations: Title predicate and six-month period differ from GRWM views. Does not establish uploader numbers, content creator profits or a change in popularity.

claims.text: YouTube's February 2026 NFL-related video report says over 30% of its 2025 global NFL-content views occurred between the conclusion of the Super Bowl and the start of the regular season, while annual global uploads of NFL-related videos grew by over 400% from 2020 to 2025.
claims.limitations: Offseason share is within the 2025 NFL-related YouTube view event population, not people; it is not season-over-season growth. Uploads and views use different units, intermediate annual data are absent, and source-defined related-video classification is not independently replicated.

claims.text: ThoughtLeaders' October 15, 2026 index detected sponsor-style reads in 176,686 long-form videos published September 15–October 14, or 6.1% of roughly 2.9 million scanned long-form uploads; the prior 30-day share was 5.9% and the year-prior share was 4.8%.
claims.limitations: Commercial detection index, not a platform-wide probability sample. Creator codes and promotional reads need not represent contracted or paid advertising; sample-channel mix changes and Shorts are excluded.

claims.text: ThoughtLeaders' September 15–October 14, 2026 scanned long-form video categories report detected-sponsor shares ranging from 1.9% in news/politics to 15.0% in health/fitness, while gaming had 37,093 detected sponsored videos at 8.6% of scanned gaming uploads.
claims.limitations: Conditional shares within each vendor-defined channel category; not probability of earning sponsor revenue for a new creator, confirmed contract counts, spend or creator profit.

claims.text: SponsorRadar reports 660,985 detected YouTube sponsor placements for February 2025–January 2026, including 147,964 gaming placements and 66,217 education placements in its indexed sample, with coverage densest on larger channels.
claims.limitations: Detected placements, not actual signed contracts or payout transactions. Its 12-month category counts cannot be combined with ThoughtLeaders' 30-day counts; growing sample coverage prevents straightforward time-series growth inference.

claims.text: Upfluence's Q1 2026 platform report covers 17,288 creator applications and 2,605 brand campaigns, with the share of applications in fashion/apparel rising from 6.2% in January to 12.8% in March; these are cross-platform applications, not YouTube sponsorship revenue.
claims.limitations: A commercial platform's market-specific applicant mix and campaign tags; not all creators, YouTube-only projects, or probability-weighted brand demand.

claims.text: AIR Media-Tech reports monthly upload medians and 25th–75th percentile ranges from a 282-channel YouTube Analytics-access study: small gaming channels 3 (2–8), medium gaming channels 10 (4–19), and medium educational channels 26 (13–31) uploads per month.
claims.limitations: Partner/selected owner-access channels and size-specific niche groups; not an all-new-creator cadence population or causal RPM effect. Percentiles describe this vendor sample.

claims.text: vidIQ's July 2026 report grouped 10,210,278 channels with at least 1,000 subscribers by average monthly uploads from April 2025 through March 2026, reporting median monthly view growth of 0.53% below one upload and 2.18% at 12 or more.
claims.limitations: Includes Shorts and long-form, excludes channels below 1,000 subscribers; observational association confounded by established channels, content formats, teams and demand, not evidence that frequency causes growth.

claims.text: A 2026 niche-specific publishing-cadence table drawn from 282 owner-Analytics channels is not directly comparable to a 10.2-million-channel index combining Shorts and long-form uploads at an at-least-1,000-subscriber entry threshold.
claims.limitations: Neither study establishes median uploads among all first-time publishers, the marginal profit of an extra upload, or matched per-channel format-specific labor hours.

claims.text: Streams Charts reports 43,692,090 hours watched across tracked live-streaming platforms during the first week of Resident Evil: Requiem in H1 2026, with week-two watch hours 68.8% below launch week.
claims.limitations: All tracked live-streaming platforms combined, not YouTube Gaming alone, not unique viewers, Shorts or nonlive views; week-two decline is title-specific, not platform-wide.

claims.text: Streams Charts reports 9,537,065 cross-platform livestream hours watched in Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream's debut week and a 9.2% decline in week two, while counted streaming channels rose 4.2% during that second week.
claims.limitations: Selected game and publisher vendor records, not independent YouTube-only title viewing, not long-term fan growth or profit.

claims.text: Hatchet's 2025 YouTube Gaming livestream report cites 8.8 billion hours watched in 2025, up 12% versus 2024, representing about 24% of its tracked gaming livestreaming watch hours across platforms.
claims.limitations: Calendar 2025 YouTube Gaming live-video annual benchmark, not 2026 individual game release viewing or all YouTube long-form and Shorts play counts.

claims.text: YouTube's advertiser suitability rules evaluate video and metadata context, including dishonest behavior and harmful or unreliable claims. A financial education label alone does not imply approval for ads or any particular creator revenue.
claims.limitations: Advertising suitability is a channel/video-specific contextual process, not a uniform ban or fixed RPM for finance content.

claims.text: YouTube's external-link policy prohibits links to phishing or other disallowed destinations while stating affiliate links are not inherently prohibited; dedicated excessive affiliate posting can violate spam policies.
claims.limitations: Individual product eligibility, local laws, link clickability and monetization cannot be inferred from this general platform policy.

claims.text: The SEC's February 6, 2026 investor alert warns that social-media stock tips, impostor investment professionals, group chats and guaranteed return claims can be scam signals; such risks are different from descriptive financial education.
claims.limitations: Investor-protection alert, not a count of fraudulent YouTube channels, diagnosis of any creator, or a legal classification of every product mention.

claims.text: U.S. FTC endorsement guidance requires context-sensitive disclosure of material brand or affiliate relationships, which can be relevant to financial product comparisons; YouTube paid-promotion labeling is a separate platform obligation.
claims.limitations: U.S. law is not identical worldwide; a course, credit product or securities promotion may implicate additional country- and product-specific rules.

claims.text: Pew's October 2026 U.S. adult survey reports YouTube ever-use of 83% for non-Hispanic single-race White adults, 85% for Hispanic adults of any race, 84% for non-Hispanic single-race Black adults, and 95% for non-Hispanic single-race Asian adults, the last estimate representative only of English speakers.
claims.limitations: Subgroup-conditional self-reported ever-use in 5,511 total U.S. adult respondents, not percentages of all YouTube viewers or of creators; per-cell n and sampling margins are unverified. Categories follow Pew grouping and cannot be imposed on individuals or extrapolated worldwide.

claims.text: YouTube Studio's owner-facing estimatedRevenue covers several native creator-income sources after applicable platform shares and is not interchangeable with CPM, ad-only earnings or sponsor/merchandise income.
claims.limitations: Owner data require authorization, native estimated revenue may be adjusted later, and not all native revenue can be assigned to a single video; public view totals cannot determine creator payout.

claims.text: YouTube Analytics separates traffic from YouTube Search, Browse features, Suggested videos and external sources, while thumbnail impressions omit several playback surfaces; traffic source alone does not establish an evergreen earnings horizon.
claims.limitations: Video age, traffic-source window, format, analytics access, geography and measurement revision must be documented; cross-sectional source shares are not causal longevity estimates.

claims.text: YouTube's medical-misinformation policy addresses high-risk prevention or treatment misinformation conflicting with local health authority guidance and may consider educational or documentary context; it can apply to external links as well as videos.
