claims.limitations: The existence of the policy does not classify all exercise or diet instruction as medical treatment or establish enforcement statistics.

claims.text: YouTube's eating disorder policy differentiates awareness and recovery content from content promoting eating disorders or self-harm, and may consider contextual age restrictions or removal.
claims.limitations: Context-specific policy judgement is not a blanket permission or a measured suitability rate for fitness creators.

claims.text: YouTube's health search shelves and source panels are geographically and linguistically limited optional discovery features; qualifying health-source applicants follow professional, channel and country conditions distinct from regular YouTube publishing.
claims.limitations: Eligibility is not guaranteed acceptance, professional certification for all fitness channels, universal feature availability, additional ad revenue, or measured audience traffic.

claims.text: YouTube's advertiser-friendly guidelines can limit ads on harmful/unreliable medical claims or detailed eating-disorder triggers independently from whether the video's wider Community Guidelines permit it.
claims.limitations: Policy categories cannot be transformed into average RPM, rejection rates or earnings projections without observed data.

claims.text: YouTube reported more than 50 million views in Japan of videos related to Splatoon 2 in the first seven days surrounding its July 21, 2017 release.
claims.limitations: Historical Japanese seven-day related-video views, not unique fans, global game sales, normalized views per creator, or evidence that platform-wide users increased.

claims.text: YouTube reported more than 93 million global video views on GTA VI Trailer 1 during December 4–5, 2023, and separately reported over 250 million views of GTA VI-related videos for that period.
claims.limitations: This was a 2023 trailer pre-release event, not the videogame's release. The single-video count and broad related-video count overlap; the latter is not additional distinct viewers.

claims.text: Ofcom's May 2026 UK child-media survey reports that among children aged 3–5 who watch videos on any app/site, 80% watch cartoons or animation, 43% funny videos and 38% learning content; among video watchers aged 8–17, 62% watch funny videos, 46% music videos and 43% gameplay content.
claims.limitations: Cross-video-platform child survey, not YouTube-only viewing or unique people. 3–5 observations are parent/guardian reported, older child observations direct; per-module subgroup sample sizes and uncertainty not extracted.

claims.text: Ofcom's 2026 UK report describes boys as more likely than girls to watch gameplay and sports videos across video apps/sites, while girls are more likely to watch music, how-to, ASMR and self-improvement videos.
claims.limitations: Qualitative direction reported for child video-sharing app use across platforms. No YouTube-specific gender-by-format rate, biological-sex inference, subgroup counts or causal explanation can be derived.

claims.text: Ofcom reports that in 2025, UK children aged 4–15 averaged 7h07 per week of YouTube viewing captured in in-home measurement, with ages 4–9 at 6h47 and ages 10–15 at 7h27.
claims.limitations: Barb in-home device measurement, not all-device total including out-of-home or mobile-network viewing. Does not identify gender by YouTube genre, children from other regions or individual minors.

claims.text: Pew's December 2025 U.S. teen survey (n=1,458, ages 13–17) finds 94% of boys versus 89% of girls report ever using YouTube; 20% of boys versus 13% of girls say they visit almost constantly.
claims.limitations: U.S. self-reported teen YouTube platform use, not a YouTube-specific video-format or topic audience, different geography and frame from Ofcom UK child video-category measures.

claims.text: In Roy Morgan's April–December 2025 Young Australians Survey of 1,129 children aged 6–13, 89% were estimated to watch YouTube; among child YouTube watchers the reported leading genres were gaming (53%), animation (37%) and comedy (36%).
claims.limitations: Australia-only 2025 survey, 89% is the publisher's estimate for the age range and genre percentages condition on YouTube watchers. Per-group sample denominators, confidence intervals, unique overlapping genres and exact national child-count precision remain unverified.

claims.text: Roy Morgan's Australian 2025 YouTube-watching children aged 6–13 survey reported gender-specific genre-use rates: gaming 67% boys versus 39% girls, fashion 5% boys versus 31% girls, and animation 38% boys versus 36% girls.
claims.limitations: Percentages condition on YouTube-watching children within each survey boy/girl group; they are not the composition of the genre audience, not inherent traits or individual identities, and do not generalize outside Australian ages 6–13.

claims.text: Within Roy Morgan's 2025 Australian child YouTube-watching survey, music was reported by 41% of girls versus 27% of boys, animals 44% versus 25%, and cooking 24% versus 14%.
claims.limitations: Girls and boys are reported survey groups; category selections overlap; exact group respondent counts and margins of error unavailable, no causal explanation or prediction for individuals.

claims.text: A 2025 analysis of English-language YouTube politics channels reports approximately half of observed comments came from just over 2% of the commenters in its study sample.
claims.limitations: Based on the paper's selected anglophone political YouTube scope, not all platform commenters, all political categories, a unique user census or the composition of political opinion. Rounded fraction and population unit retained.

claims.text: The journal-formatted full text of a 2025 observational sample of English-language political YouTube channels reports higher average Perspective API toxicity scores among the more prolific commenters, while a Cardiff bibliographic landing-page abstract states the reverse. Mercata follows the manuscript's analysis and Figure 11, with this contradiction disclosed.
claims.limitations: This is a selected observational sample, not all viewers or channels. The coded model has measurement error and potential bias; no behavioral causality, individual risk profile, political identity or global toxicity rate follows. The bibliographic abstract conflicts with the primary PDF.

claims.text: A 2026 analysis of 129 selected English-language climate-change YouTube videos found a higher proportion of positive attitudes among reply-thread conversations than independent top-level comments.
claims.limitations: Videos selected via March 2021 search results and restricted by English content, minimum comments and scientific-consensus criteria; observational association not proof that replying causes positivity or a result for all YouTube communities.

claims.text: The selected 129-video climate study found presenter type and solution-versus-blame framing were associated with differences in coded comment attitudes in the analyzed sample.
claims.limitations: Associations within narrow subject sample, automated sentiment classifier and manual coding; no proof of causal persuasion, user demographics, gender/political identity, or optimal messaging strategy.

claims.text: Tubular Labs' 2025 report analyzes a panel of 74,276 U.S. female viewers aged 25–34 who engaged at least five times with YouTube Gaming content between July 2024 and June 2025; it reports strong affinities with selected Beauty channels.
claims.limitations: Vendor-selected panel, age and gender segmentation method and selection probabilities not published in an auditable microdata sample; selected repeat Gaming engagers are not all U.S. female viewers or all beauty/gaming audiences.

claims.text: A Tubular Labs 2025 figure labels only 5% overlap between selected Beauty content and the specified U.S. female age-25–34 YouTube Gaming audience, but does not expose the exact matched-person intersection or clarify the percentage base enough to derive an audience union.
claims.limitations: Provider-reported descriptive figure only; do not interpret as share of all gamers, all beauty viewers, universal gender preference, or an exact number of overlapping people. Missing methodology prevents independently computing unique union.

claims.text: YouTube may suppress age/gender cells in owner Analytics with low traffic or narrow filtering; unpublished thresholds mean unavailable demographic data do not establish zero viewers.
claims.limitations: Owner-only aggregated metrics are not public competitor data or a worldwide viewer census.

claims.text: YouTube Analytics API documentation defines gender dimensions for logged-in viewers under female, male and user-specified reporting categories.
claims.limitations: Not individually verified sex or identity, not demographics of signed-out viewers, not creator gender or a cross-community census.

claims.text: Ofcom's 2026 Children and Parents report, using Barb in-home measures, finds UK ages 4–15 averaged 7h07 of YouTube viewing per week during 2025 (up 8% on 2024), with ages 4–9 averaging 6h47 and ages 10–15 7h27. This is annual observation, not a measured holiday or school-term contrast.
claims.limitations: Barb in-home broadband-connected viewing only; content genre and holiday/term seasonal subdivisions not available from these annual averages. Age bases overlap and survey modes are distinct.

claims.text: Current YouTube general and paid-service terms identify Google LLC as the service provider under the cited contract scope; they do not by themselves identify every local payment, ad sales or tax entity.
claims.limitations: Legal provider identity is conditional on applicable territory and terms; no separate global corporate-history conclusion.

claims.text: YouTube distinguishes advertiser-funded creator revenue shares, paid viewer subscriptions and purchases, and claims held by content rights holders, so a viewer, advertiser, creator, buyer and rightsholder are not interchangeable economic units.
claims.limitations: Structural map, not measured income or transaction prevalence. An uploader need not monetize and an ad-viewer need not be the advertiser paying.

claims.text: YouTube Studio's owner-facing 'When your viewers are on YouTube' report shows the channel's audience online across YouTube in the preceding 28 days, and is offered as a guide for live and Premiere scheduling.
claims.limitations: Channel owner data are not publicly available for competitors and do not contain a reliable universal time-zone breakdown or long-term causal lift estimate.

claims.text: YouTube Studio scheduling can make a private upload public at a chosen local date, time and time zone; a strike can block scheduled publication and the watch-page publication date may reflect Pacific Standard Time.
claims.limitations: Time-zone choice does not establish where viewers live, which hour maximizes revenue, or immunity from daylight-saving or scheduling mistakes.

claims.text: YouTube's performance FAQ says publishing while an audience is active can aid early views, but upload time is not known to affect long-term video performance; live and Premiere broadcasts have different timing needs.
claims.limitations: Publisher guidance is not a randomized cross-country causal test, and channel-specific timing outcomes are unmeasured.

claims.text: YouTube warns that geography breakdowns may omit low-volume countries for privacy or system reasons; a report total can exceed the sum of displayed geographic rows, and realtime/private/unlisted video geography is unavailable.
claims.limitations: Suppressed geography cannot be coded as zero or as an absence of viewers, and exact suppression thresholds are unpublished.

claims.text: Video comments can be moderated, held, paused, disabled or highlighted; visible comments are neither verified purchase reviews nor an unbiased sample of viewers.
claims.limitations: Based on documented features and exclusions, not measured creator switching costs, migration outcomes or revenue effects; unlisted data-transfer options remain unassessed.

claims.text: Studio distinguishes subscribers, returning viewers and monthly unique channel viewers. These measures are not a transferable customer contact record.
claims.limitations: Based on documented features and exclusions, not measured creator switching costs, migration outcomes or revenue effects; unlisted data-transfer options remain unassessed.

claims.text: YouTube documents conditional download of uploaded videos and separately a Brand Account channel transfer that risks losing destination content; these features do not establish export of followers or reviews to another platform.
claims.limitations: Based on documented features and exclusions, not measured creator switching costs, migration outcomes or revenue effects; unlisted data-transfer options remain unassessed.

claims.text: YouTube's official membership guidance allows up to six channel membership levels and notes that viewer price schedules differ by country and member sign-up timing. Published price options are not measured actual channel prices.
claims.limitations: Policy documentation does not provide merchant cohort prices, conversion rates, refund incidence, effective seller margins or buyer-level transaction observations. Fees and methods vary by region and channel.

claims.text: A canceled channel membership normally remains accessible until the end of its billing cycle without refund of the unused part; separate support or Apple-purchase procedures may apply to faults or payment disputes.
claims.limitations: Policy documentation does not provide merchant cohort prices, conversion rates, refund incidence, effective seller margins or buyer-level transaction observations. Fees and methods vary by region and channel.

claims.text: YouTube describes Super Chat, Super Stickers and Super Thanks as voluntary, generally non-refundable payments, while unauthorized charges have a reporting path.
claims.limitations: Policy documentation does not provide merchant cohort prices, conversion rates, refund incidence, effective seller margins or buyer-level transaction observations. Fees and methods vary by region and channel.

claims.text: For YouTube Shopping transactions completed on external retailer or marketplace sites, the merchant determines final price, fees and taxes and handles payment, fulfillment, returns and refunds, not YouTube.
claims.limitations: Policy documentation does not provide merchant cohort prices, conversion rates, refund incidence, effective seller margins or buyer-level transaction observations. Fees and methods vary by region and channel.

claims.text: YouTube Studio distinguishes total members with perk access, active noncanceled subscriptions, membership gains/cancellations, access-expired lost members and transactions containing new signups or recurrences; billing periods may span 28, 30 or 31 days, so aggregate counts alone do not establish the renewal rate of a matched entry cohort.
claims.limitations: Official metric definitions, not owner-authorized member-level history or a representative channel sample. Calculating cohort renewal requires actual due dates, aligned entries and settlement outcomes.

claims.text: A creator with advanced feature access can select one of their public or unlisted Videos, Shorts or Live streams as a clickable related video below a Short's channel handle; the feature is not proof that viewers clicked or continued watching.
claims.limitations: Owner ability to use the feature and geographic/device visibility may vary; no link-level click population or conversion rate obtained.

claims.text: YouTube Studio includes format-specific traffic reports and an across-formats viewer-overlap report, but neither its general views nor overlapping audiences independently establishes a Short-to-long-form referral or an individual linked viewing path.
claims.limitations: Analytics report availability and exact export dimensions vary. Viewer overlap is undirected; causal gain, click attribution and source-specific economic return remain unknown.

claims.text: Since August 24, 2026, YouTube's public playback-start view measure applies to Shorts, ordinary videos and Live, while YPP earnings/eligibility retain distinct engaged or qualified view/hour measures; their numerators cannot be pooled into a single funnel conversion rate.
claims.limitations: Mixed-format and pre/post-revision counts require compatible epochs and separate counting units; no real creator observed.

claims.text: In Pew's U.S. adult February-March 2025 daily-use survey (n=5,123), 48% said they visit YouTube at least daily and 33% said several times daily; this survey percentage is neither a deduplicated daily global user count nor the same survey base as Pew's 84% ever-use prevalence.
claims.limitations: Self-reported U.S. adults only, with frequency response categories rather than server-measured users; adjacent ever-use sample n=5,022 surveyed February-June 2025.

claims.text: GWI's DataReportal April 2026 global past-month YouTube use figures are 55.3% of surveyed internet users aged 16+ including China and Russia, versus 70.6% for a different covered-market sample excluding them; neither is a verified count of distinct monthly YouTube users worldwide.
claims.limitations: Survey prevalence among covered internet users not platform account logs, not all residents or children, and the two geographic populations differ.

claims.text: Late-2025 YouTube advertiser planning estimates reported in DataReportal's 2026 country reports describe 85 million ad-reachable people/accounts in Mexico, 254 million in the US and 150 million in Brazil; they do not establish monthly platform users or deduplicated cross-country people.
claims.limitations: Google advertising-planner addressable estimates, subject to planning assumptions, age targeting and methodology changes; adult male/female ratios are for the adult ad audience and no summed global census is derived.

claims.text: In Pew's 2026 5,511-adult U.S. use survey, 85% of respondents classified under the published 'Men' subgroup and 83% under 'Women' reported ever using YouTube. These are percentages of each survey subgroup, not the composition of YouTube users or biological sex counts.
claims.limitations: The published categorical table does not establish biological-sex-specific YouTube use or subgroup-specific sample sizes, error margins or activity frequency.

claims.text: Pew's distinct August 24-30, 2026 survey of 5,166 U.S. adults reports regular YouTube news consumption for 41% of men, 28% of women, and 39%, 38%, 33% and 26% of four successive published adult age groups. These are within-subgroup percentages of U.S. adults, not viewer composition or content creator identity.
claims.limitations: The news-frequency measure is different from ever using YouTube; precise subgroup denominators/uncertainty and cross-tabs by gender x age are not supplied here.

claims.text: Pew's 2026 news fact sheet lists 23%, 22%, 25%, 26%, 32%, 35% and 34% of U.S. adults reporting regular news from YouTube in survey years 2020-2026, respectively. The observed descriptive series is not a panel of the same people and does not establish a trend's cause or a platform-wide video view count.
claims.limitations: Survey designs and response context require year-specific interpretation; year-to-year changes are not asserted significant without sampling uncertainty, and these values are not total YouTube MAU or channel-level news demand.

claims.text: YouTube's current upload disclosure guidance requires creators to label realistic content that is generated or meaningfully altered using AI, including fabricated depictions of actual people or events and AI-generated music featured as the main content; minor or fantastical edits are distinguished.
claims.limitations: Describes official published rules and feature-gate documentation, not individual legal advice, measured claim prevalence, successful monetization, creator income or automatically adjudicated copyright ownership.

claims.text: YouTube states that disclosing AI use alone does not reduce audience reach or automatically remove monetization eligibility, while nondisclosure of qualifying content can prompt labeling or penalties. Eligibility remains subject to separate partner and content policies.
claims.limitations: Describes official published rules and feature-gate documentation, not individual legal advice, measured claim prevalence, successful monetization, creator income or automatically adjudicated copyright ownership.

claims.text: YouTube's July 15, 2025 'inauthentic content' policy rename clarifies that repetitive or mass-produced material may be ineligible for YPP monetization; the publisher described this as a clarification of existing standards, not a ban on all AI-assisted creation.
claims.limitations: Describes official published rules and feature-gate documentation, not individual legal advice, measured claim prevalence, successful monetization, creator income or automatically adjudicated copyright ownership.

claims.text: YouTube describes an experimental, country-limited likeness-detection feature available only to eligible adult channel owners/managers after identity and face-video verification; detected matches may be reviewed and submitted to a privacy complaint process.
claims.limitations: Describes official published rules and feature-gate documentation, not individual legal advice, measured claim prevalence, successful monetization, creator income or automatically adjudicated copyright ownership.

claims.text: YouTube's copyright help notes that human authorship and legal protection of AI-created work vary by jurisdiction and that an AI-related takedown may need further details; presence or absence of AI disclosure is not a determination of copyright ownership.
claims.limitations: Describes official published rules and feature-gate documentation, not individual legal advice, measured claim prevalence, successful monetization, creator income or automatically adjudicated copyright ownership.

claims.text: YouTube reported that over 80% of worldwide 2023 views on anime-related videos came from outside Japan. This is a bounded share of video viewing events, not a percentage of distinct anime fans, countries with active creators or creator profit.
claims.limitations: The publisher did not specify query taxonomy, total view denominator, split by video formats, the number of unique viewers or a comparable post-2026-view-revision series.

claims.text: Separate selected online animation-fan surveys in April 2025 reported U.S. ages 14-24 n=358 weekly YouTube animated series watching (63%) and Mexico ages 14-24 n=379 weekly animated meme watching (84%). Different questions cannot rank countries' overall animation watching.
claims.limitations: These are survey total n, not guaranteed item-specific response denominators; fans were the screened population, not all users, creators or the entire age cohort.

claims.text: YouTube identifies watch history as a principal signal for personalized Home recommendations and the currently watched video as a main signal for Up Next suggestions; their exact relative signal weights are not published.
claims.limitations: Official feature documentation does not establish causal creator income effects, exact ranking factors, newcomer channel success probability or platform-wide experiment results.

claims.text: YouTube Search weighs query relevance in title, description and content and engagement; Shorts discovery has its own personalized feed and other surfaces. YouTube states no minimum Shorts upload cadence is required.
claims.limitations: Official feature documentation does not establish causal creator income effects, exact ranking factors, newcomer channel success probability or platform-wide experiment results.

claims.text: YouTube's Shorts creator guide states Shorts performance does not intrinsically harm recommendations for ordinary videos; this is a current publisher description, not a measured universal causal study of creator revenue.
claims.limitations: Official feature documentation does not establish causal creator income effects, exact ranking factors, newcomer channel success probability or platform-wide experiment results.

claims.text: In vidIQ's July 20, 2026 snapshot, 24,813,187 of 61,186,246 indexed channels with at least one public subscriber had at least 1,000 subscribers; 4,836,743 had at least 10,000 and 792,376 at least 100,000. These are cumulative counts within the provider's covered sample.
claims.limitations: Vendor-selected public channel index excludes zero-subscriber, deleted or unindexed channels and does not identify channel owners, paid creators or a platform census.

claims.text: vidIQ separately tracked 11,752,034 indexed channels that started with at least one subscriber and increased their public video count over the trailing 90 days ending July 20, 2026; the channel counts and median subscriber growth by starting tier do not enumerate unique people or all active creators.
claims.limitations: Net published-video-count change can undercount uploads offset by removals or visibility changes, and selection excludes channels without this positive change.

claims.text: In vidIQ's September 2026 study of 32,926,088 indexed channels starting under 1,000 subscribers with at least one video 360 days earlier, a total of 500,409 ended at 1,000 or more. Observed threshold rates rose across groups with larger nonnegative net video-count changes, without matching baseline age or creator resources.
claims.limitations: Not new-creator entrants, not a random YouTube channel census; excludes unavailable/negative-count histories. Observational correlation is not an upload cause or YPP eligibility rate.

claims.text: A 2026 research preprint examines 107 keyword-discovered daily-life vlog channels selected by first upload dates between November 2025 and August 2026; 51.4% never reached 1,000 lifetime views by its September snapshot, and 11.2% had three or fewer uploads. This is not a probability sample of all new creators.
claims.limitations: Author preprint, restricted keyword-discovered vlog genres and variable follow-up; modeled monetary return, estimated labor and event-study association do not verify individual payouts, profit or causal generalization.

claims.text: The preprint reports USD 1.61 median hypothetical long-form advertising value across those 107 channels using an assumed USD 2.30 RPM. Its 185 median work hours use an assumed three labor hours per finished video minute; neither represents observed YouTube payouts, expenses, profit or actual recorded work time.
claims.limitations: Author preprint, restricted keyword-discovered vlog genres and variable follow-up; modeled monetary return, estimated labor and event-study association do not verify individual payouts, profit or causal generalization.

claims.text: In the separately selected 420-channel video-history dataset, the preprint reports 56,419 videos and a roughly 164.2% association between a channel's first breakout and subsequent views, not a randomized causal estimate of earning or an all-channel recommendation formula.
claims.limitations: Author preprint, restricted keyword-discovered vlog genres and variable follow-up; modeled monetary return, estimated labor and event-study association do not verify individual payouts, profit or causal generalization.

claims.text: YouTube's link-sharing Help says normal URLs in Shorts descriptions and comments are non-clickable, whereas external URLs in long-form video descriptions and comments can be clickable if channel advanced features are enabled.
claims.limitations: Specific surfaces have exceptions, such as clickable related-video links in Shorts and Shopping affiliate links; actual channel feature status, locale, device and link performance are not verified.

claims.text: YouTube allows creator profile links and creator-pinned comments but documents separate display constraints and advanced-feature access for clickable external links; pinned comment exposure on mobile requires opening the comments section.
claims.limitations: No uniform click exposure, view-to-buyer conversion, revenue or causal advantage of placing a link has been measured.

claims.text: YouTube's external-links policy covers links in videos, audio, comments and descriptions and forbids links to Community Guidelines-violating destinations. Ordinary affiliate linking is not inherently a violation, but excessive affiliate-focused spam may violate platform rules.
claims.limitations: Policy eligibility is conditional and does not guarantee a specific product's compliance, checkout effectiveness or commercial payout.

claims.text: YouTube's key-moments audience retention report is a video-level creator Studio Analytics feature, typically processing after 1–2 days; highlighted retention moments require sufficient qualifying video duration and views and do not appear as public video statistics.
claims.limitations: Availability, advanced segments and processing vary; no owner-authorized cohort analytics were collected. Does not supply public channel-wide completion rates.

claims.text: YouTube Studio labels 'Stayed to watch' for Shorts as the share of times viewers stayed past the first seconds rather than swiping away. Engaged views exclude loops, and average duration/percentage viewed are computed among engaged-view events; none independently supplies the percentage completing the entire Short.
claims.limitations: Measurement definitions apply to current Studio guidance and can vary by metric epoch; public Shorts views are not a valid denominator for a fabricated completed-viewer rate.

claims.text: An audience-retention segment may record more segment views than overall video views because a viewer can watch that segment repeatedly. A retention spike is not necessarily new distinct viewers or proof of positive sentiment.
claims.limitations: No actual segment-level owner data, view-person deduplication or sampled completion curve collected.

claims.text: The Studio Trends tab identifies saved/audience topics and Shorts content gaps over a recent 28-day window. Its interest categories are not observed absolute monthly search counts or buying customers.
claims.limitations: Documented official mechanics, no actual query panel, keyword volume, distinct users, revenue or causal creator outcome.

claims.text: Google Trends can filter to YouTube Search and displays sampled search interest normalized to a 0–100 index within a geography, time range and comparison frame, not the number of monthly searches.
claims.limitations: Documented official mechanics, no actual query panel, keyword volume, distinct users, revenue or causal creator outcome.

claims.text: YouTube search suggestions may vary by user history, typed term, location and regional trends, and cannot establish population search frequencies.
claims.limitations: Documented official mechanics, no actual query panel, keyword volume, distinct users, revenue or causal creator outcome.

claims.text: YouTube Shorts guidance says creators can record, edit and upload a Short using a smartphone without specialized equipment; this does not establish that every creator owns a suitable device or has zero labor and network costs.
claims.limitations: Platform documentation gives production constraints, not a market-cost sample, verified cash outlays, typical labor hours or net earnings.

claims.text: YouTube says the video player adapts to 16:9, square and vertical videos and recommends avoiding baked-in black bars; this does not imply the same production time, eligibility rules or revenue for vertical and horizontal output.
claims.limitations: Platform documentation gives production constraints, not a market-cost sample, verified cash outlays, typical labor hours or net earnings.

claims.text: YouTube supports mobile, webcam and encoder live-stream methods, with eligibility and setup conditions; streaming guidance recommends preserving approximately 20% additional outbound bandwidth and planning encoding, test and monitoring work.
claims.limitations: Platform documentation gives production constraints, not a market-cost sample, verified cash outlays, typical labor hours or net earnings.

claims.text: YouTube's general Terms preserve ownership of creators' own uploaded content while granting YouTube a worldwide, non-exclusive service license; this does not automatically entitle a creator to payments.
claims.limitations: Documentation-only: no verified creator contracts, territorial legal opinions, royalty splits, actual claims or payout amounts.

claims.text: Content ID reference use requires exclusive rights in each claimed territory, so non-exclusively licensed stock media, public-domain works and CC BY materials are not eligible exclusive matching references.
claims.limitations: Documentation-only: no verified creator contracts, territorial legal opinions, royalty splits, actual claims or payout amounts.

claims.text: YouTube offers a CC BY license choice for eligible owned uploads, allowing reuse with attribution; this broad reuse grant does not convey exclusive Content ID rights and the CC option is unavailable for videos with active Content ID claims.
claims.limitations: Documentation-only: no verified creator contracts, territorial legal opinions, royalty splits, actual claims or payout amounts.

claims.text: Copyright matches can be blocked, monetized or tracked, potentially with different policies by territory; claim status alone does not prove a copyright strike or net cash income to a particular creator.
claims.limitations: Documentation-only: no verified creator contracts, territorial legal opinions, royalty splits, actual claims or payout amounts.

claims.text: YouTube prohibits artificially increasing views, likes, comments or subscribers; hiring a third-party promoter does not exempt the channel from violations performed on its behalf.
claims.limitations: No sampled creator exposure/financial outcomes or independent enforcement statistics; policy categories are not measured incident counts.

claims.text: YouTube warns that fake sponsorship or brand-deal attachments and websites can deliver malware or steal creator credentials. It advises independent sponsor verification, passkeys, two-step verification, and reviewing delegated channel permissions.
claims.limitations: No sampled creator exposure/financial outcomes or independent enforcement statistics; policy categories are not measured incident counts.

claims.text: YouTube's spam/scam policy covers misleading off-platform diversion, repetitive deceptive posts, artificial engagement and fake job, investment or support offers. Ordinary requests to like or subscribe are not automatically violations.
claims.limitations: No sampled creator exposure/financial outcomes or independent enforcement statistics; policy categories are not measured incident counts.

claims.text: Official creator-safety and phishing guidance gives precautions but does not provide a representative YouTube creator-level annual probability of hack, scam losses, deceptive sponsorship incidence or paid growth-fraud prevalence.
claims.limitations: No sampled creator exposure/financial outcomes or independent enforcement statistics; policy categories are not measured incident counts.

claims.text: Google advertiser-planner YouTube reach reported for India in late 2025 was 500 million, with the published end-2024 to late-2025 change +9 million (+1.8%). Ad reach is not monthly active users or a confirmed change in real viewers.
claims.limitations: Advertising planner estimates can be revised and may differ from active person counts; this is not an income or creator estimate.

claims.text: Google advertiser-planner YouTube reach reported for Indonesia in late 2025 was 151 million, with the published end-2024 to late-2025 change +8 million (+5.6%). Ad reach is not monthly active users or a confirmed change in real viewers.
claims.limitations: Advertising planner estimates can be revised and may differ from active person counts; this is not an income or creator estimate.

claims.text: Google advertiser-planner YouTube reach reported for Japan in late 2025 was 78.5 million, with the published end-2024 to late-2025 change -0.2 million (-0.3%). Ad reach is not monthly active users or a confirmed change in real viewers.
claims.limitations: Advertising planner estimates can be revised and may differ from active person counts; this is not an income or creator estimate.

claims.text: Google advertiser-planner YouTube reach reported for Philippines in late 2025 was 59.6 million, with the published end-2024 to late-2025 change +1.9 million (+3.3%). Ad reach is not monthly active users or a confirmed change in real viewers.
claims.limitations: Advertising planner estimates can be revised and may differ from active person counts; this is not an income or creator estimate.

claims.text: ShortSync's October 16, 2026 vendor report counts 199,276 successful cross-platform posts from 66,318 uploaded videos by 6,175 tool users. Its upload-level table reports 76% posted to multiple platforms; this tool-user rate is not a population-wide YouTube creator multihoming percentage.
claims.limitations: Publisher explicitly warns of self-selection toward cross-posters, failed/draft and imported-account history exclusion, variable monthly observation windows, and a rolling page whose numbers can change.

claims.text: In ShortSync's October 16 snapshot, YouTube accounts for 18% of successful post events; among multi-platform uploads, 56% include an Instagram+YouTube pair and 55% a TikTok+YouTube pair. Posting the same video to two platforms does not establish that any viewer moved between them.
claims.limitations: Multiple pairs can describe the same upload and are not disjoint. Post shares are not user/audience shares, and no deduplicated view or cross-service consumer journey is observed.

claims.text: Abolfathi's peer-reviewed YouTube–Twitch analysis uses Twitch Prime's September 2016 exposure change to compare single-platform and dual-platform creator behavior; it reports lower relative production effort and weaker outcomes for multihomers after the shock, rather than an unconditional advantage to cross-posting.
claims.limitations: Historical gaming-streaming context and identification assumptions limit transport to 2026 Shorts cross-posting. The paper does not measure an actual creator's cross-platform follower migration or monetization conversion.

claims.text: Stream Hatchet/Streamlabs tracked 2.22 billion YouTube Gaming watched hours in Q1 2026 and 1.79 billion in Q2, a reported 19.3% quarterly decline; these are tracked gaming livestream viewer-hours, not unique people or publisher revenue.
claims.limitations: Commercial third-party tracking with report-specific categories and rounded numbers. Not a census of actual people, income, cross-platform migration or causality.

claims.text: Stream Hatchet/Streamlabs reported 1.07 million distinct YouTube Gaming broadcasting channels in Q1 2026 and 878,000 in Q2; a channel is neither a unique creator-owner nor a verified monetized publisher.
claims.limitations: Commercial third-party tracking with report-specific categories and rounded numbers. Not a census of actual people, income, cross-platform migration or causality.

claims.text: The Q2 2026 report separately presents 12.97 billion watched hours for general YouTube Live, up 2.7% quarter-over-quarter, and 1.79 billion for YouTube Gaming, down 19.3%; the classification must not be collapsed to one identical gaming audience.
claims.limitations: Commercial third-party tracking with report-specific categories and rounded numbers. Not a census of actual people, income, cross-platform migration or causality.

claims.text: Omdia's January 2026 industry release estimates that music videos accounted for 33% of overall YouTube viewing time in its analysis. This is a viewing-time share, not a fraction of unique users, song uploads or creator receipts.
claims.limitations: Omdia methodological scope and independently verifiable denominators are not fully specified in the public press release; category share does not measure music-creator profitability.

claims.text: YouTube's weekly Top Songs combines official music video, user-made soundtrack and lyric video viewing, while Top Songs on Shorts ranks songs by how many Shorts were made using them, not by all YouTube music plays; these metrics are not interchangeable.
claims.limitations: Chart eligibility, country, ranking window and publisher policies matter. Song view totals can include content uploaded by creators other than rights holders.

claims.text: YouTube Music Insights ranks attributed song or artist interest by official and user-generated video views but excludes Shorts views; Content ID holders may monetize, track or block matching videos in different countries.
claims.limitations: Music-chart audience activity is not identical to artist ownership, paid music subscribers, royalty distribution or creator net revenue.

claims.text: CreatorIQ's creator campaign payment report states that the top 10% of creators paid through its system received 62% of recorded 2025 creator payment volume, versus 60% in 2024 and 53% in 2023. This is concentration among payees, not all creator earnings or YouTube receipts.
claims.limitations: Commercial payment intermediary data, campaigns and participating brands may change year to year; no verified independent probability sampling, nonpaying creators, or YouTube-only group denominators.

claims.text: CreatorIQ's direct-payment study reports a top 1% payee share of 21% in 2025 (18% in 2024, 15% in 2023), while the bottom 90% of 2025 payee creators received 38%; category group shares are on recipient payment volume, not views or numbers of videos.
claims.limitations: Payee identity/denominator limited to vendor-managed campaigns and positive disbursements; historical comparability unknown; not a longitudinal all-YouTube creator earnings panel.

claims.text: CreatorIQ's press release contrasts a reported USD 11.4k average per campaign with a USD 3k median creator earnings figure. Because those statistics have different entity denominators, dividing them or comparing as like-for-like mean versus median is unsound.
claims.limitations: Source methodology does not fully align campaign average and individual payee median; unit mismatch must remain visible, and neither amount accounts for YouTube native receipts or creator labor/cash costs.

claims.text: CreatorDB's June 2026 dataset covered 2,153,140 indexed YouTube channels with at least 1,000 subscribers, including 601,232 with 100,000+; these are provider index counts, not all channels, distinct owners, paid creators or an all-YouTube census.
claims.limitations: Unknown inclusion and refresh probabilities for smaller channels and deleted accounts; vendor asserts high large-tier coverage but it is not independently audited.

claims.text: CreatorDB reports 30-day median subscriber growth of approximately 0.7% for indexed channel tiers above 10,000 subscribers, with only 0.5–0.89% of analyzed channels in those tiers increasing by more than 10% during its sampled 30 days.
claims.limitations: Not a birth cohort or multiple-window trend, proprietary subscriber snapshots can be rounded, and the groups are established indexed channels, not new entrants.

claims.text: Within CreatorDB's June 2026 indexed channels with >=1,000 subscribers, primary category counts include 322,869 People & Blogs, 222,645 Gaming, 198,440 Education, and 196,340 Music. These are selected category assignments for channels, not numbers of active videos, unique viewers or buyers.
claims.limitations: The index’s broad primary-category taxonomy excludes other overlapping interests, channel coverage and completeness differ by genre, and category counts do not measure demand or profitability.

claims.text: In a YouTuber cohort studied by Panjwani and Xiong (2026), monthly Patreon receipts fell 33.59% from the treated group's prior baseline around disclosure and extortion following the 2015 Patreon cyberattack. This is a historical conditional-group change, not a platform-wide decline or a verified counterfactual income effect.
claims.limitations: 2026 journal publication analyzes 2015-era shock and selected early/later Patreon adopting YouTubers; precise study sample counts and standard errors unconfirmed from publisher text, and results are not universal content-policy or profit estimates.

claims.text: The paper's conservative difference-in-differences robustness estimate finds a 7.7% reduction in monthly YouTube video output among sampled creators after the Patreon subscription-revenue shock relative to later Patreon joiners, with output depressed through seven post-shock months. Causal interpretation depends on the natural-experiment design assumptions.
claims.limitations: 2026 journal publication analyzes 2015-era shock and selected early/later Patreon adopting YouTubers; precise study sample counts and standard errors unconfirmed from publisher text, and results are not universal content-policy or profit estimates.

claims.text: After the sampled Patreon revenue shock, affected YouTubers increased affiliate promotion and sponsored-content incidence while the paper found no significant rise in ad-break frequency proxied by crossing a historical 10-minute duration threshold. The paper reports top-decile viewed channels favored sponsorship while lower-view channels favored affiliate links; neither proves incremental profit.
claims.limitations: 2026 journal publication analyzes 2015-era shock and selected early/later Patreon adopting YouTubers; precise study sample counts and standard errors unconfirmed from publisher text, and results are not universal content-policy or profit estimates.

claims.text: The study did not find statistically significant adverse viewership or engagement effects accompanying increased affiliate and sponsorship advertising in its historical treated creator comparison. Nonsignificance does not establish zero effect or predict audience response to present-day promotions.
claims.limitations: 2026 journal publication analyzes 2015-era shock and selected early/later Patreon adopting YouTubers; precise study sample counts and standard errors unconfirmed from publisher text, and results are not universal content-policy or profit estimates.

claims.text: YouTube's reused-content monetization rules list meaningful critical commentary, explained sports replays, original rewritten movie dialogue and reaction videos with commentary as potentially acceptable examples. They are not automatic monetization approvals and independent copyright restrictions still apply.
claims.limitations: Platform-wide examples are not an adjudication of any individual channel, work, music track, license, country-specific fair use or verified earnings.

claims.text: YouTube explicitly separates its channel-level reused-content monetization rule from copyright ownership and fair use: even permission from an original rights holder does not ensure a minimally altered compilation meets YPP originality requirements.
claims.limitations: Platform-wide examples are not an adjudication of any individual channel, work, music track, license, country-specific fair use or verified earnings.

claims.text: Content ID can block, monetize, or track matched videos depending on rightsholder settings, sometimes by country or region; a claim does not automatically prove infringement or resolve a local copyright exception.
claims.limitations: Platform-wide examples are not an adjudication of any individual channel, work, music track, license, country-specific fair use or verified earnings.

claims.text: YouTube's July 15, 2025 clarification renamed its repetitive-content YPP policy to inauthentic content without changing the reused-content rule for commentary, reactions, clips and compilations.
claims.limitations: Platform-wide examples are not an adjudication of any individual channel, work, music track, license, country-specific fair use or verified earnings.

claims.text: IFT's Mexico ENCCA 2024 reports 55% of all surveyed respondents used online audiovisual media, while YouTube was selected by 66% of the subgroup consuming online audiovisual media; these are different denominators, neither a national YouTube MAU count.
claims.limitations: The published regulator summary does not provide the conditional platform question's item count, individual respondent records, unique monthly users, YPP creator population or a harmonized 2015-to-2024 YouTube series.

claims.text: IFT ENCCA 2024 compared 26% of surveyed people consuming online audiovisual content in 2015 to 55% in 2024. The difference is for online audiovisual consumption generally; survey instrument and population differences must be checked before deriving any YouTube-specific longitudinal estimate.
claims.limitations: The published regulator summary does not provide the conditional platform question's item count, individual respondent records, unique monthly users, YPP creator population or a harmonized 2015-to-2024 YouTube series.

claims.text: ENCCA 2024 surveyed 8,750 people, 6,125 urban and 2,625 rural. Its named audiovisual platforms include YouTube 66%, Netflix 32%, TikTok 29%, Facebook 29%, and Disney+ 13% among the online audiovisual group; multiple platform selections overlap.
claims.limitations: The published regulator summary does not provide the conditional platform question's item count, individual respondent records, unique monthly users, YPP creator population or a harmonized 2015-to-2024 YouTube series.

claims.text: Oxford Economics fielded separate creator, business and user surveys in January–March 2026. YouTube recruited the creator sample; 6,100 U.S. and 43,300 India creator responses are sample counts, not respective national creator populations.
claims.limitations: Non-probability creator recruitment does not cover an identifiable population of all uploaders or zero earners; sample mixing with other studies is invalid.

claims.text: Oxford Economics lists 12,100 EU27 creator responses plus separate France (1,100) and Germany (1,400) rows. Because France and Germany fall within EU27, the regional rows are not independent additive geographic populations.
claims.limitations: Publication does not provide respondent-level country IDs or cross-row deduplication, so the country table is not a global population estimator.

claims.text: YouTube's published 2025 U.S. economic-impact estimates exceed USD 60 billion in GDP and 540,000 supported full-time-equivalent jobs. The underlying Oxford model includes downstream effects and an eight-hour-week filter for creator work in its FTE component; neither number is a creator earnings distribution.
claims.limitations: Commissioned macroeconomic estimates use modeled downstream effects, YouTube-provided aggregate payout information and survey-based off-platform revenue estimates; individual receipts, zero-earner counts and hours are unavailable.

claims.text: Alphabet's FY2025 SEC filing separately reports YouTube advertising revenue of USD 31.510B for 2023, USD 36.147B for 2024 and USD 40.367B for 2025. These are annual corporate revenues, not amounts paid to creators.
claims.limitations: No per-creator payout distribution, subscription allocation, unique audience count or cost information; the adjacent Google subscriptions category bundles products outside YouTube.

claims.text: Alphabet's Q2 2026 SEC filing reports YouTube ad revenue of USD 11.055B in Q2 2026 versus USD 9.796B in Q2 2025, and USD 20.938B in H1 2026 versus USD 18.723B in H1 2025. Q2 is included in each corresponding half-year, so the figures are not additive.
claims.limitations: Unaudited interim corporate revenue in different time windows, not full-year 2026 revenue, direct creator receipts, payouts, engagement or income.

claims.text: The annual YouTube advertising revenue line increased about 14.72% from 2023 to 2024 and 11.67% from 2024 to 2025; Q2 2026 and H1 2026 can be compared only against the corresponding prior-year calendar windows.
claims.limitations: Simple nominal USD revenue growth, not inflation-adjusted, causal effects, viewership growth, creator earnings growth, or all-stream YouTube revenue.

claims.text: Alphabet's February 2026 SEC-furnished earnings release reports that 2025 YouTube advertising-plus-subscription revenue exceeded USD 60 billion. Given separately reported 2025 YouTube advertising revenue of USD 40.367 billion, the broad subscription component implied by those two annual statements is greater than USD 19.633 billion, not an exact figure or verified channel-membership revenue.
claims.limitations: The strict bound includes YouTube subscription categories with different economics, including consumer services and television; neither subscriptions nor creator payments are separately itemized in the SEC revenue table. This is not the similarly sized commissioned U.S. GDP economic-impact estimate.

claims.text: YouTube reports aggregate payments of roughly or more than USD 100 billion to global creators, artists and media companies over four-year windows, with an explicit January 2021–December 2024 window on its official artist page and a later rolling-four-year statement in its January 2026 CEO letter.
claims.limitations: Different or overlapping four-year windows and rounded/threshold disclosures. Includes companies and rightsholders; cannot determine unique individual recipients or creator-income distribution.

claims.text: YouTube for Artists reports USD 8 billion paid to the music industry from July 2024 through June 2025, including possible rights owners and intermediaries. This overlaps and is not additive to broad creator, artist and media-company distribution figures.
claims.limitations: Music industry payout total is first-party, rounded, and not evidence of net incomes directly received by individual musicians, independent creators or channel members.

claims.text: The YouTube-published Oxford 2024 U.S. impact headline was above USD 55B GDP contribution and roughly 490K FTE jobs, versus above USD 60B and above 540K in the 2025 impact headline. Because these are rounded or lower-bound modeled quantities with potentially changing estimation methods, no actual growth rate can be calculated from them.
claims.limitations: Different published years and modeling methods must not be assumed strictly comparable. Economic GDP value added and modeled supported FTE are not corporate revenues, YouTube payments or creator income.

claims.text: Eligible desktop YouTube Studio creators can test up to three title, thumbnail or combined variants concurrently; results are judged by watch-time share, not click-through rate, and an inconclusive test is not evidence of performance uplift.
claims.limitations: No per-channel testing outcomes or creator revenue are supplied by the public Help page.

claims.text: YouTube's native A/B tool excludes Shorts, active Premieres, scheduled live events, videos made for kids, mature or private videos; eligible archived livestreams and converted concluded Premieres may qualify.
claims.limitations: Requires advanced features and desktop owner access, which were not accessed for this study.

claims.text: YouTube's authorized playlist reports distinguish aggregate activity for channel-owned videos from activity in a playlist that may contain other owners' videos.
claims.limitations: Official definitions only; no creator analytics queried.

claims.text: Playlist starts, views per playlist start and average time in playlist are restricted to web-initiated playlist usage and cannot measure all-device unique viewers or series completion.
claims.limitations: No available private watch histories, repeated-person cohort data or buyer events.

claims.text: A peer-reviewed CHI 2025 study of 1,923 selected VTubers reports historical public Super Chat-derived monthly mean USD 2,667 versus median USD 127, a sampled 25% of channels with no recorded Super Chat, and 2018/2023 between-VTuber Gini estimates near 0.60/0.75.
claims.limitations: 2017–July 2023 selected public VTuber archives; no verified after-fee take-home, all-creator zero-earner denominator or production costs. Study authors' 'income' measure is limited to visible financial traces.

claims.text: Among roughly 6.75 million accounts posting public chat messages in the selected VTuber cohort, 7.96% sent a Super Chat and 12.65% held at least one channel membership. The groups can overlap, and the denominator excludes viewers who never chatted.
claims.limitations: Historical selected public chat-posting account frame, not all viewers, unique offline people, causal membership conversion or total paying audience share.

claims.text: A November 2025 peer-reviewed study modeled 92,412 filtered YouTube live-chat messages from 397 selected videos (780 hours) after screening a larger 673,551-message/1,957-video corpus; its peer-versus-video emotional influence estimate is model-based rather than an experimental causal effect.
claims.limitations: English and message-rate selection; model-classified non-exclusive labels are not user self-reports; no viewer or creator payout population estimated.

claims.text: YouTube distinguishes filtered Top chat from less filtered Live Chat displays; edited livestream archives lose chat replay, and live polls are not available in replay. These visibility conditions obstruct treating visible messages as a complete archive of all participants.
claims.limitations: Moderation and privacy protections also affect available display data; no participant-level records are collected.

claims.text: The published YTLive sample contains more than 507,000 five-minute concurrent-viewer observations across 12,156 selected YouTube livestreams in May–June 2024, with recorded broadcast durations and hashed stream identifiers.
claims.limitations: Stream-level and five-minute concurrency only; neither distinct viewers nor watch-person sessions, donations, Shorts, VOD or net creator income.

claims.text: YTLive's 2024 selected livestream analysis reports descriptive daypart/weekend and broadcast-length differences in sampled concurrent viewership, not experimentally verified optimal times, guaranteed creator engagement or monetization outcomes.
claims.limitations: Limited May–June 2024 selection, uncontrolled stream category, channel size and geographic differences; no cause or financial benefit can be inferred.

claims.text: YouTube's October 2025 shopping research selected 5,000 top-purchased products in H1 2025 and 1,000 transaction-ranked tagged videos from another 60-day 2025 window; a separate April 2025 U.S. Gen Z survey of 500 people recorded 61% agreeing YouTube helped discover unfamiliar brands/products. None supplies a universal buyer conversion rate.
claims.limitations: Ranked company-selected products/videos are not totals of purchases or buyers; survey reports discovery opinions among online Gen Z ages 14–24, not tracked sales.

claims.text: Google Merchant Center YouTube affiliate reports distinguish merchant-tag clicks, order events, gross and net sales, and commissions; several include pending transactions and hybrid fixed fees. Merchant analytics are restricted account data rather than public creator profit statistics.
claims.limitations: No merchant account or transaction data accessed; privacy thresholds hide small groups and prohibit re-identification, dataset joins and sensitive inference.

claims.text: Across more than 10,000 vendor-selected paid YouTube sponsor integrations, Agentio reports 38% of sponsored-video views after day 30, 27% after day 90, and roughly 30% of attributable clicks after day 30. View-share age windows overlap, and clicks are separate events, not buyers.
claims.limitations: Vendor-selected paid client placements, dates and late windows vary; no universe of unpaid creators, absolute purchase rate or payee profit.

claims.text: Agentio's sponsored integrations dataset reports repeat same-creator relationships with approximately 1.8x eighth-placement CTR and 1.9x sixth-placement conversion rate relative to earlier placements, and a reported 54% decline in continuing advertiser cumulative CPM after one year.
claims.limitations: Selected renewing relationships are non-random survivors; reported multiples lack absolute event baselines and verified randomized causal attribution; advertiser CPM is not creator wages or take-home profit.

claims.text: EMARKETER attributes Agentio's playbook evidence to more than 10,000 paid creator integrations from October 2023 through December 2025, with about 92% of sampled creators based in the U.S.; this is a vendor-specific sponsorship market rather than representative global YouTube creator income.
claims.limitations: Geography shares are rounded and may not sum to exactly 100%; downstream revenue, zero earners and all-platform opportunities remain unknown.

claims.text: An August 21 Agentio report predicted approximately 30% higher public video views under YouTube's Aug 24 counting change using a presumed 30-second retention proxy in 35,800 selected June–July long-form videos; it did not directly observe a postchange long-form engaged-view conversion.
claims.limitations: Unpublished YouTube organic engaged threshold, selected vendor client cohort, assumed early attention period and distinct smaller Shorts sample; a modeled projection is not observed actual growth.

claims.text: After Aug 24, a separate Agentio report measured about 549M public playback-start events and 330M engaged-view events across more than 75,000 connected-creator videos, reporting an approximately 60% engaged-to-public share in that selected sample.
claims.limitations: Provider-selected videos published after June 1; event totals rounded and time window limited. No deduplicated people, all-platform ratio, causal traffic growth or after-cost creator payout estimates.

claims.text: In Agentio's selected postchange videos, feed/browse views had approximately 20% engagement versus 85% on watch pages, with browse contributing 77% of the *non-engaged view gap*; those shares do not equal unique people, creator monetization, or the distribution of all YouTube content views.
claims.limitations: Vendor-specific surface definition, non-random permissioned creators, rounded rates; 77% of non-engaged gap is not share of all public views.

claims.text: YouTube's standard AdSense payments cycle distinguishes previous-month finalized earnings added to an account on days 7–12, payment eligibility on day 20, a possible issued transfer during days 21–26 and actual later bank receipt. None of these equals individual creator profit or income per work hour.
claims.limitations: Timing assumes a standard compliant AdSense for YouTube account and its actual reporting currency, with no unpaid holds; issued or projected settlement must not be presented as observed bank cash.

claims.text: YouTube's Commerce Product Module allocates 70% of eligible net membership, Super Chat and Super Sticker receipts to partners, while live Gifts under the separate Virtual Items Module earn Rubies at USD 0.01 per Ruby (one Ruby per two redeemed Jewels). The formulas use different denominators and must not be combined.
claims.limitations: A viewer Jewel purchase is not a redeemed gift or a confirmed creator balance; net Commerce excludes taxes and certain fees. Eligibility, actual transfers and creator profit remain unknown.

claims.text: YouTube's current Gifts setup instructions say eligible vertical and horizontal livestreams can use Jewels-powered gifts. It remains subject to Virtual Items module acceptance, region, stream and child-directed restrictions; older vertical-only policy wording does not describe the full current documented surface.
claims.limitations: No individual channel eligibility checked; current Gifts availability, exact supported effects and reporting rules can change.

claims.text: YouTube excludes Super Chat and Super Stickers from private, unlisted, age-restricted, made-for-kids and fundraising videos and when live chat/comments are unavailable, independent of follower or audience counts.
claims.limitations: Published feature restrictions are not an account-specific ruling or measured monetization rate.

claims.text: The official YouTube video resource distinguishes defaultLanguage (language of the video's title and description) from defaultAudioLanguage (language in the video's default spoken audio). Translations, dubbing and country-of-viewing are different units and do not count unique language speakers.
claims.limitations: Public metadata may be missing and sample selection biased. No worldwide YouTube language-person denominator or public speaker distribution is available.

claims.text: YouTube's official captions.list API returns language-labeled track metadata rather than transcripts, requires authorized access, and documents a 50-unit query quota. It does not disclose the fraction of viewers using each subtitle language.
claims.limitations: No authorization, caption track enumeration, downloads, or user-level data were collected for the Mercata language protocol.

claims.text: YouTube public Posts can include text, images, GIFs, polls, quizzes and videos and may appear in channel Posts, Home, Subscriptions and eligible image-specific Shorts feeds. This does not guarantee that every subscriber or distinct viewer sees the Post.
claims.limitations: Posts are ineligible for supervised accounts and not publicly visible on made-for-kids channels; no public global Post impression or member population is available.

claims.text: The documented YouTube Data API commentThreads.list endpoint enumerates comment threads associated with videos/channels, subject to pagination, 100-item page limits and possible missing replies, but does not establish a complete Creator Posts or Communities sampling API.
claims.limitations: No API calls or individual comments gathered. Cannot infer all submitted posts, community membership, suppressed comments, audience size or creator earnings.

claims.text: A February 2026 STEM educational video study summarized 124 Spanish-language physics/engineering videos from 2019–2025 on one YouTube channel. Its selected Analytics cohort found greater retention in science-dissemination than exercise videos and associations with shorter durations and fixed introductions.
claims.limitations: Publisher abstract only. One selected owner-channel cohort, nonrandom duration/intro allocation, 30-second retention and average duration not comparable with public like/view counter outcomes, and no creator profit.

claims.text: A March 2025 Indonesian educational YouTube study sampled 139 of 218 videos on one channel by proportional category sampling and reported more views/shares on instruction videos but higher likes and watch durations on practice-test content.
claims.limitations: One creator channel with different viewing purpose by category, no controlled randomized content assignment, representative population or earnings.

claims.text: A September 2025 Turkish educational YouTube study considered 126 highly viewed mathematics videos and found no statistically significant video-length correlation with recorded public views, likes or comments.
claims.limitations: Selected successful-visibility population and public reaction counters, not creator income, unique learning cohorts, session duration, or a platform-wide optimal video length.

claims.text: A peer-reviewed 2026 ICWSM archival research dataset collected 446,971 YouTube Trending captures across 104 countries from July 2022 through June 2025, yielding roughly 78.4 million ranked entries representing 726,627 unique video IDs. Trending pages were retired in July 2025.
claims.limitations: Former platform-selected ranked-list snapshots, not a representative video population or all viewers; repeated video appearances across periods and countries prevent entry count being a unique-user or upload total.

claims.text: In YouTube's April 2026 commissioned NRG U.S. online survey of 496 respondents aged 14–29, 78% perceived memes as widely known; 71% reported watching fandom story explainers and 69% reported watching self-described niche community content.
claims.limitations: Survey question about perceived popularity is not a watching-rate denominator; niche and lore responses overlap and do not count all users, unique viewers or creators globally.

claims.text: YouTube Analytics country dimension attributes activity and authorized monetized owner estimated revenue to a viewer's country, not to the creator's own residence, passport, payout address or tax country.
claims.limitations: Only authorized monetized owner reports may expose monetary metrics; missing country attribution and restrictions cannot be filled from public channel metadata.

claims.text: YouTube documents potential suppression of country-related viewer metrics but states revenue-by-geography data is not limited; monetary country reports still require authorized YPP access and do not supply representative creator distributions.
claims.limitations: No private channel report, creator-residence panel or zero-earner information was retrieved.

claims.text: Country-specific YouTube access and actual AdSense payment currency thresholds must not be inferred from the viewer geography; international individual income comparisons additionally require dated real receipts and private-consumption purchasing-power methods, distinct from nominal FX and GDP PPP.
claims.limitations: No observed owner settlement currencies, country-specific creator earnings, actual FX/PPP rates, withholding or local cash expenses are available.

claims.text: YouTube documents 70% of eligible net memberships and Supers revenue for relevant Commerce products, with sales tax and applicable fees excluded before allocation; YouTube currently covers credit card processing transaction costs, not an extra creator-assessed rate.
claims.limitations: Individual MCN agreements, sales-tax breakdowns, payout currency conversion, withholding and producer expenses remain account-specific.

claims.text: Google's Shopify YouTube Shopping affiliate terms describe a configurable 30–50-day pending commission period, a recommended 30-day last-click attribution window and next-month merchant billing for locked transactions. Returns can reverse pending commission amounts.
claims.limitations: Merchant-side accounting instructions may not apply to all merchants, countries or creator agreements; pending, locked and merchant-billed commissions do not document actual creator bank deposits.

claims.text: AIR Media-Tech's June 2025 study of advertiser CPM data from more than 3,000 vendor-associated YouTube channels reported sample prices of USD 14.67 for U.S. audiences, USD 8.91 for U.K. audiences and USD 0.74 for India per 1,000 advertising impressions, among its 20 highest and 20 lowest listed markets.
claims.limitations: Non-probability provider sample; country-specific sample counts, time-window detail and average/median aggregation not given. Advertiser gross CPM is not creator RPM, all-creator net income or creator residence.

claims.text: The examined AIR June 2025 published highest and lowest country CPM lists do not state a Mexico CPM; this omitted rate cannot be imputed, and the 2025 ad-impression prices cannot be converted into a typical creator's income or purchasing-power equivalent.
claims.limitations: Omission from a selected extremes table is not zero advertising revenue or evidence that a country is unmonetized; the vendor's managed clients may overlap other AIR channel studies.

claims.text: YouTube Studio Trends shows recently watched and audience-related top searches over roughly 28 days, with ordinal audience interest and country/language/device availability limits; it is not an absolute count of monthly keyword searches or a creator profit forecast.
claims.limitations: Private channel-derived audience relevance can vary with saved searches and country. No account data was retrieved.

claims.text: Official owner Reach and Analytics API reports can separate YouTube Search, Browse, Suggested and external video view events. The documented traffic-source API has a 50,000 queried-video-days limit, enabling bounded prospective age-window comparisons but not publicly verified tutorial evergreen earnings.
claims.limitations: Owner authorization required; no empirical long-tail cohort was accessed. Suppressed or unobserved data are not zeros, and raw lifetime views are not age-normalized.

claims.text: AIR's October 2026 reuse of its selected 300 monetized-client channels reports 58% of sampled ad revenue in the top 30 ranked channels, 82% in the top 75 and 96% in the top 150, with the bottom 150 accounting for 4%. These are overlapping percentile groups within one selected advertiser-funded revenue cohort.
claims.limitations: Already monetized participating AIR clients, not all YouTube creator income, no zero-earner population, sponsorship receipts, costs, taxes or labor hours.

claims.text: Across AIR's same 300 monetized channels and 3,595 selected channel-months in May 2025–May 2026, its published calendar-month median RPM values were USD 1.56 in January and USD 2.35 in November; distinct 10K–100K and 100K–10M subscriber groups had selected median RPM of USD 2.14 and USD 2.04 respectively.
claims.limitations: Monthly published medians are not matched panel estimates of all creator earnings or causal seasonal effects, and subscriber counts are not view counts, unique channels per month, net income or wages.

claims.text: One YouTube photography creator published self-logged time for 61 completed videos, with mean 9.74, median 7.37 and range 1.87–60.92 labor hours per published video; postproduction accounted for approximately 50% of averaged logged time.
claims.limitations: Single author, completed-video survivor sample and unverified self logging; not creator-population production hours or actual earnings.

claims.text: The same selected creator's author diary reported 169 mean and 147 median minutes of labor per finished video minute, and the six individually rounded stage means sum to 9.73 hours against a separately reported overall 9.74-hour mean.
claims.limitations: Means of stage fields were rounded; ratio of work minutes per published minute is neither an industry standard nor a payout-per-hour estimate.

claims.text: Adobe Express surveyed 384 U.S. cross-platform video creators via Prolific in December 2025: 71% reported using AI video tools, 41% of those tool users used them weekly, and 74% of YouTube-posting respondents said they used AI.
claims.limitations: Commercial vendor recruitment, selected self-reports, overlapping multi-platform posting, subgroup denominators and no independent adoption audit.

claims.text: In the same Adobe Express survey, 56% reported saving more than 30 minutes per video using AI tools, while 10% reported saving more than four hours; the four-hour threshold is a nested subgroup, not a separate independent group or stopwatch-verified gain.
claims.limitations: Retrospective self-reported time saving across platforms without actual matched logs, causal comparison, subscription costs or measured creator profit.

claims.text: YouTube Content ID claims may track, block, or monetize matched videos by geography, with an optional rightsholder revenue share rather than a fixed uploader entitlement. For initial disputes filed within five days, held monetization revenue is withheld from the original claim day; later filing starts holding on the dispute date. Held money is later allocated to the appropriate party, not automatically the creator.
claims.limitations: Official platform rules only; not proof of legal infringement, a given account's rights, actual creator bank receipts, legal costs, revenue share percentage or expected net profit.

claims.text: For a Content ID initial dispute YouTube gives the claimant up to 30 days to respond, but an eligible reinstated-claim appeal or an eligible blocking claim escalated directly to appeal gives seven days. A valid copyright removal request is separate from a Content ID match and can lead to a strike; the response periods are not payment schedules.
claims.limitations: YouTube Studio procedures, not verification of any person's rights or likelihood of outcomes; no recovered revenue, creator profit, typical case cost or successful appeal count.

claims.text: YouTube officially lists standard and expanded YPP geographic access and AdSense for YouTube payment methods for selected countries, but account approval, reporting currency, individual payment methods and feature-specific monetization are independent checks. Copyright rightsholders can impose video-specific geographic Content ID policies rather than a universal country-level earnings rate.
claims.limitations: Based on documented Mexico/US/UK country-list snapshots only; no account data, nationality-based tax, approved feature counts, personal income or specific territory claim data.

claims.text: BFI's 2024 video-essay poll named 183 unique works nominated by 47 voters, including 70 YouTube-published selected works averaging 36 minutes and 56 Vimeo-published works averaging 11 minutes. More than 70% of the selected YouTube works linked external support services; these are curated counts and link presence, not creator income or viewer retention.
claims.limitations: Selection on expert favorites, cross-platform publication and nominated videos, not all creators; no representative upload cadence, labor or paid patron conversions.

claims.text: YouTube reports more than 200 million global view events for videos related to video essays during calendar 2024, a different observation frame from BFI's 183 expert-nominated works; their counts, person denominators and economic outcomes cannot be combined.
claims.limitations: Official related-video classification is not publicly reproduced here and describes view events, not unique users, channel count or a typical essay's views.

claims.text: Public vidIQ subscriber and video-count cohorts do not contain the owner-only thumbnail impression denominator required for YouTube Studio impressions CTR; the selected 32.9 million-channel under-1k cohort also cannot be treated as a group of verified first-time creators. A valid new-creator discovery study must stratify known entry age, content format and comparable exposure windows.
claims.limitations: This is a documented measurement and sampling design. No owner-authorized Reach data, representative new-creator success probabilities, buyer conversions or income were obtained.

claims.text: YouTube's official genre editorials describe more than six billion GRWM-title video views globally January 1–June 5, 2023, over 25 million prom-and-GRWM title views during 2024, and over 100 million beginner sewing-machine title-related views during 2025. These are unlike event windows and content filters, not an additive audience, trend estimate, or a gender-specific viewer population.
claims.limitations: No uniquely counted viewers, buyer receipts, average creator earnings, comparable same-category growth, validated audience gender or representative channel counts.

claims.text: YouTube channel creation and standard publishing require an authorized Google Account and channel, but the official setup instructions do not mandate a newly purchased camera, software license, or ad campaign.
