Intermediate features can require phone verification; neither publishing nor verification establishes YPP eligibility or a creator cash payout.
claims.limitations: Official minimum publishing path only; all operating costs, labor, individual approvals and future income remain unmeasured.

claims.text: YouTube's official livestream guidance requires verified channel status, no livestream restriction within 90 days and minimum age 16; mobile livestreaming additionally requires at least 50 subscribers and eligible mobile OS, with possible audience limits below 1,000 subscribers and up to 24 hours for initial activation.
claims.limitations: Mobile restrictions do not apply to ordinary uploads and can vary by account; no individual's channel eligibility, audience or live income is observed.

claims.text: YouTube's AdSense for YouTube program requires an adult payee aged at least 18. An otherwise eligible under-18 creator may link a parent/guardian's approved AdSense for YouTube account, with payments received by the adult rather than the minor. Neither arrangement guarantees a channel's monetization approval.
claims.limitations: Account linking and identity compliance remain conditional; no user's identity, guardianship, jurisdiction, payout or bank details collected.

claims.text: YouTube's published supervision policy requires parental supervision to create or maintain a channel in Brazil for users under 16. This jurisdiction-specific account gate is distinct from its age-16 live streaming floor and its age-18 direct AdSense payment rule.
claims.limitations: No general country-by-country age catalog supplied, and a compliant supervised channel still must satisfy content, feature and payment eligibility. The Brazil requirement must not be generalized worldwide.

claims.text: YouTube Studio permits owner-supplied captions by timed file, supported transcript auto-sync or manual editing, while automatic caption generation uses speech recognition in supported languages and may contain accent, dialect, overlap and noise errors.
claims.limitations: Feature documentation only; not a per-language caption availability count, measured transcript accuracy or a population survey.

claims.text: YouTube has separate creator workflows for localized video titles/descriptions, creator-provided alternate audio, and conditionally available automatic dubbed speech; source-target language, rights, content and video length can restrict automatic dubbing, including videos over 120 minutes.
claims.limitations: No owner Studio permissions or translated audience reports were accessed; availability differs per video and neither a localization option nor a viewer preference establishes new sales or reach.

claims.text: YouTube states its YPP application decision is typically provided in about one month once a channel is in review, with possible queue or repeated-review delays; neither qualifying subscriber/view thresholds nor passing time makes acceptance automatic.
claims.limitations: Typical review timing is an indicative service period, not a fixed maximum or guarantee of payout; no applicant records or observed processing durations collected.

claims.text: YouTube documents a 21-day appeal window for YPP application rejection, first-rejection reapplication after 30 days, and repeat-rejection reapplication after 90 days. Appeal response is stated within 14 days, and success may lead to YPP approval/readmission within 30 days, subject to channel policy review.
claims.limitations: Different time origins: rejection notice versus appeal submission; appeal/suspension-specific exceptions exist. None guarantees program acceptance, actual earnings, or bank settlement.

claims.text: Nielsen The Gauge reports that YouTube represented 13.8% of all US TV-set viewing time in May 2026, 14.2% in July and 15.8% in August, with all-streaming TV shares of 48.6%, 49.0% and 49.6% in the same months.
claims.limitations: TV-device US persons 2+ viewing-time denominator; not mobile traffic, total unique users, monetized views or creator income; the dates May and July are not adjacent months.

claims.text: YouTube gained 1.6 percentage points of reported US TV viewing share between July and August 2026 in Nielsen's TV set sample; this percentage-point change does not measure changes in YouTube's mobile usage, overall YouTube unique visitors or creator revenue.
claims.limitations: Seasonality, World Cup programming and school calendar affect the TV denominator; no cross-device causal comparison or viewership panel across individual screens is supplied.

claims.text: YouTube stated it had over one billion monthly active podcast viewers as of January 2025 and more than 700 million hours of podcast viewing on living-room devices in October 2025, compared with about 400 million in October 2024. Monthly people and TV watch hours are distinct units.
claims.limitations: First-party platform press figures; no public cross-device deduplication method or precise session minutes per person, creator revenue or comparable universal viewer census.

claims.text: YouTube reported over 800 million podcast viewing hours among Premium users in April 2026. Edison independently reported that in Q3 2025, 82% of U.S. weekly podcast consumers watched video podcasts and 78% listened to audio-only podcasts, overlapping behaviors rather than exclusive population groups.
claims.limitations: Premium paid-user product watch hours and Edison US weekly survey respondents use different frames and cannot be added to October living-room watch hours or used to estimate creator income.

claims.text: YouTube defines a podcast show as a playlist of episode videos, while a separately eligible RSS importer can create static-image videos from authorized audio feeds; manually uploading an MP3 alone is not ordinary video uploading and the RSS path does not syndicate to outside providers.
claims.limitations: RSS available in selected countries with verification, no channel access checked or actual published podcast catalog sampled.

claims.text: YouTube says eligible podcasts can be available in YouTube Music with audio-only or background playback, and most do not require a Music Premium subscription; supporting Shorts and copyright-claimed or otherwise ineligible playlists may not receive podcast features.
claims.limitations: 'Most' is not all creators, tracks, territories or devices; no platform share of audio-only users or creator earnings observed.

claims.text: YouTube's Watch Page Monetization Module provides a 55% share of eligible net watch-page advertising revenue; the Analytics API's grossRevenue is an advertiser-side gross estimate and cannot be multiplied by 55% to infer creator earnings without the undisclosed eligible net accounting base.
claims.limitations: Requires module acceptance, rights and ad eligibility. No channel-authorized gross-to-net reconciliation, actual payout or creator cost ledger was obtained.

claims.text: YouTube permits mid-roll ad slots on eligible monetized long-form videos at least eight minutes long, but manual or automated opportunities do not guarantee a served ad impression, income or incremental profit.
claims.limitations: Slot placement and serving decisions vary; no impression logs, ad fill, viewer responses or earnings experiments were accessed.

claims.text: The published YouTube Premium creator guidance allocates revenue using eligible member viewing, including background playback and downloads when later recorded online, and requires suitable Watch Page or Shorts modules. It provides no fixed payout per Premium view.
claims.limitations: No channel-owner data, member pool size or creator allocation share; paid platform viewers cannot be equated with a creator's channel-membership customers.

claims.text: YouTube Shorts ads revenue is pooled per eligible country after music-cost allocation and distributed based on monetizing creators' eligible engaged-view shares. Creators receive 45% of their allocated country pool, not of raw public video views or gross advertiser receipts.
claims.limitations: No actual country creator-pool balance or all qualified viewer denominators; module acceptance, rights and ad suitability remain necessary.

claims.text: YouTube announced that beginning February 1, 2027 a separate 45%-of-eligible-net targeted Shorts ad route can apply to channel groups of five or fewer, distinct from pooled Shorts Feed ad payments, with a separate 90-day rolling qualified view gate.
claims.limitations: Future eligibility is not a current 2026 payout. Individual targeted ad net amounts, engaged-view qualification and settled creator income are unknown.

claims.text: YouTube Analytics liveOrOnDemand separates view events during a live broadcast from view events outside it for a given livestream video. The compatible report supports views and watch minutes, but not averageViewPercentage when liveOrOnDemand is included.
claims.limitations: No authorized creator analytics or distinct-person retention or revenue observations were collected.

claims.text: YouTube's streaming archive rules say broadcasts under 12 hours can be automatically archived, while ones over 12 hours might not be captured; editing a live archive removes chat replay. Missing archives are not evidence of zero viewing demand.
claims.limitations: Archive availability, privacy and editor activity select which live broadcasts can be compared after the fact.

claims.text: Pew's Aug. 24–30 2026 survey of 5,166 U.S. adults reports 34% regularly get news on YouTube, including 35% of Republican/lean-Republican adults and 36% of Democratic/lean-Democratic adults within their respective subgroups; this does not describe any specific channel's audience party composition.
claims.limitations: Self-reported U.S. adults, party-specific denominator; not verified individual viewers, other countries, political behavior, creator pay or statistical significance of small differences.

claims.text: YouTube Data API search.list supports geographic, language-relevance and publication-window discovery filters but does not supply an exhaustive upload census or unique viewers; Google Trends provides normalized Google Search interest and cannot be interpreted as absolute YouTube searches or political support.
claims.limitations: Event panel was not executed; index values must stay scoped to request frame and no causal event effect or individual political inference is supported.

claims.text: YouTube's public video metadata language, default audio track language and public comment text are separate fields and observation units; public commentThreads and comments endpoints enumerate published comment events with pagination but do not provide the viewer's spoken language or all reply/user participation denominators.
claims.limitations: No actual comments or persons were collected. Moderator deletions, disabled comments, code-switching, metadata gaps and sample choice prevent estimating total YouTube users by language or sensitive user identities.

claims.text: Pew's representative 2023–24 U.S. Religious Landscape Study (n=36,908) reports 23% of adults watched religious services online or on TV at least monthly (16% at least weekly). Its question did not distinguish YouTube from television or other digital sources, so no YouTube-specific religious audience share follows.
claims.limitations: A self-reported broad-media survey cannot identify individual viewer religions, YouTube usage, specific channel membership, monetization or 2026 platform engagement.

claims.text: Google's 2006 closing of its YouTube acquisition, YouTube's 2007 creator revenue-sharing launch, 2017–2018 program-entry safeguards, 2023 early fan-funding access and 2026 announcement of 2027 conditions refer to different business or eligibility events and cannot form a single unchanged creator-revenue policy.
claims.limitations: Original platform statements and company filings, not an economic creator cohort, representative payment series or causal outcome study.

claims.text: Official YouTube and Twitch support materials distinguish downloading or exporting uploaded/recorded media from migration of subscriber relationships. Vimeo OTT provides seller-side customer and transaction CSV exports with marketing opt-in fields. These are different portability units and do not establish a measured creator migration success rate.
claims.limitations: Account-specific media may be unavailable or expire; Vimeo seller CSVs carry privacy restrictions; no cross-platform follower transfer, reactivation probability, creator profit or actual buyer migration was measured.

claims.text: One self-logged photography creator's 61 published videos had a median of 7.37 and mean of 9.74 work hours, whereas three separate observational educational-video studies report limited retention, viewing or engagement measures in selected videos. These frames cannot establish universal video-quality scores, causal instructional effectiveness or creator profitability.
claims.limitations: The work diary omits unpublished projects and represents one creator; educational-video sampling has mixed owner/public analytics, nonrandom selection and no linked receipts or labor measurements.

claims.text: CreatorDB's June 2026 indexed primary-category counts cannot be converted into audiences-per-creator using global title-filtered video upload or view events, or percentages measured among 358 selected U.S. animation fans in 2025. These sources have differing unit, inclusion, geography and population denominators.
claims.limitations: Three mismatched illustrative pairs do not measure active niche creators, platform-wide unique viewing people, profitability, demand or scarcity; no ratio is reported.

claims.text: In separate 2025–26 observational frames, Click Analytic reports 57% nonactive within a prior 30-day vendor-defined window among approximately 1.9 million indexed established YouTube accounts, while an independently sampled set of 3,375 website-linked company video channels reports 46% without public uploads in 90 days and 27% without uploads in a year. In a third vidIQ below-1,000-subscriber sample, zero net public-video-count changes do not prove no uploads. None measures permanent creator exit.
claims.limitations: Samples have different publisher selection rules, channel-size cohorts, periods and activity definitions. Company channels are not people; no closures, first-entrant denominators or actual creator income are validated.

claims.text: For made-for-kids YouTube content, personalized advertising and several native commerce or fan-interaction features are restricted, but contextual advertising may still appear. These eligibility gates apply at different video, stream, and channel scopes; an animated style alone does not establish child-directed classification. No general creator revenue change can be calculated from the restrictions.
claims.limitations: Official policy rather than actual program approval, child audience size, video RPM, producer cost, comparative kid-animation profit or platform-wide channel coverage.

claims.text: Pew's 2026 U.S. YouTube ever-use rates by household income, education and residential community come from a 5,511-respondent adult survey and are published as separate subgroup marginals, not matched income-by-residence or income-by-education cells. A separate 5,166-person August panel measures regular YouTube news use, so neither survey's whole-sample error nor records can be assigned to joint demographic intersections.
claims.limitations: Published tables omit nonrespondents; cell n, joint weights, design effects and most intersections are unmeasured. Asian usage rate is restricted to English speakers. No personal profiles are collected.

claims.text: YouTube Analytics `subscribedStatus` reports distinguish subscribed and unsubscribed viewer activity at the time it occurs. A person may contribute views to both states after subscribing mid-period; public subscriber counts and subscriber-feed referral categories are not equivalents to this authorized owner-only view split.
claims.limitations: No actual YouTube channel analytics, subscriber/non-subscriber share, identifiable viewers, revenue, or conversion observations were obtained. Report metric, date, surface, and region conditions must match.

claims.text: A creator cash-profit range can be calculated conditionally from explicitly supplied bounds on eligible view events, creator-side ad-only revenue rates, other net receipts, cash expenses and creator labor. The resulting interval is an algebraic sensitivity envelope, not a statistically calibrated earnings confidence interval or a measured newcomer wage distribution.
claims.limitations: Mathematical model and official metric/revenue definitions; no actual channel observations, representative rate distributions, probability weights or empirical forecast validation.

claims.text: Published 2026 vendor snapshots count different kinds of YouTube channel objects: vidIQ's July index includes 61,186,246 with at least one subscriber, its 90-day selected set has 11,752,034 positive-net-public-video-count channels, and its separate 360-day endpoint cohort has 32,926,088 qualifying below-1,000-subscriber channels. CreatorDB's June index counts 2,153,140 channels with at least 1,000 subscribers. These different frames do not measure a deduplicated global active creator population or paid creator count.
claims.limitations: Coverage, thresholds, dates, visibility and publisher definitions differ; net public video count changes are not actual upload event logs, and channels may not uniquely correspond to humans, YPP approval or profit.

claims.text: Dated YouTube topic view counts for Halloween makeup and video essays, and Edison's selected U.S. weekly podcast format survey, provide distinct descriptive reasons to study possible viewer needs but cannot establish causal content format preferences, niche undersupply, advertising earnings, purchase intention or newcomer profit without separately designed and conducted research.
claims.limitations: The source sets use incompatible category and viewer definitions, selected populations, times and units; hypotheses and proposed comparisons are not observed creator experiments.

claims.text: YouTube's normal video publication settings include titles, descriptions, thumbnails and tags but are not themselves priced marketplace sales. Paid channel memberships use eligible tier prices and channel perks, while YouTube Shopping displays products linked to an external merchant store. These surfaces have different transaction, pricing, approval and payment units.
claims.limitations: Official controls, not evidence of a creator's actual sales, cost, membership enrollments, store conversion or individual net profit.

claims.text: A global Omdia estimate that 1% of videos capture 91% of viewed time cannot establish video-level concentration within an individual niche or the share of creator earnings. Those require independently defined and populated cohort denominators.
claims.limitations: Raw global analyst frame was not independently audited and no actual niche video data were collected.

claims.text: YouTube's selected 2025 multi-audio watch-time share and May 2026 dubbing language count, and late-2025 country ad-planner audience estimates, are different source populations, metrics and geography. They cannot be combined to estimate year-on-year growth of unique YouTube viewers or net creator income by language market.
claims.limitations: No linked population-by-language panel, no calibrated search volume, no language-specific unique viewer counts and no randomized dubbing outcome study.

claims.text: AIR Media-Tech's June 2026 observational study of approximately 18,000 channels offers weekly niche posting recommendations, whereas its separately selected July 2026 282-channel study reports observed monthly output quartiles and other performance metrics. These source populations and target statistics are not the same, cannot be averaged to yield optimal creator schedules, and provide no representative causal creator profit estimate.
claims.limitations: Vendor studies with selection, sponsorship and unobserved confounding risks; causal intervention, channel overlap, newbie dropout and net earnings are unmeasured.

claims.text: Public video links, formal collaborator credits and explicitly documented remixes may be recorded as directed content-reference edges; they do not reveal distinct viewers traveling between channels, meme origination, automatically shared ad revenue or causal subscriber/revenue gains.
claims.limitations: Official collaboration feature and selected editorial formats are documented, but no actual graph edges, random sample, viewer migration, income or causal origin data were collected.

claims.text: YouTube has published dated strict lower-bound upload counts for narrower title or related-topic sets: over 30,000 latte-art title videos and 300,000 origami-related videos in calendar 2024, more than 500,000 cake-decorating-related uploads in Jan–Sep 2024, more than 80,000 upcycle-title uploads in calendar 2025 and over 450,000 morning-routine-title uploads in H1 2026. Different predicates and dates prevent treating these as full or additive niche counts.
claims.limitations: Publisher aggregate lower bounds without raw sample validation, independent category deduplication, upload-channel IDs, annualization, revenue, or genre-specific all-upload denominators.

claims.text: YouTube publicly describes Shorts Remix editing and original attribution controls, selected tier-list activity exceeding one billion video view events in H1 2025, and other editorial meme/fan forms. These represent overlapping production and topic formats, not separate audience or paid creator populations. Shorts remixing and Studio Collaborations differ.
claims.limitations: Public product documentation and editorial source selected examples; no per-format creator counts, unique viewers, migration rate or revenue measured.

claims.text: Four selected Digital 2026 country reports reproduce Google's YouTube advertiser-reach estimates for October 2025 and published changes over both end-2024-to-late-2025 and July-to-October 2025. India and Japan have different change directions across these unequal windows. Such revision-sensitive ad-planner changes are neither deduplicated real viewer growth nor creator earnings.
claims.limitations: Four selected country reports only; population is addressable YouTube ad reach, not YouTube MAU/DAU, actual active humans, demographic survey panels, or channel income. Platform audience-estimation changes are not quantified.

claims.text: Google Account, YouTube channel or Brand Account, delegated creator access, viewer or subscriber, Studio owner analytics, public YouTube Data API metadata, Google Ads paid campaign billing and AdSense for YouTube payout are distinct program/role/measurement units; none permits treating channels or ad events as unique content creators or verified net earnings.
claims.limitations: Official product and permissions documentation, not linked person-level identities, actual purchaser counts or sampled creator accounting. Unique people and creator profit unmeasured.

claims.text: YouTube Analytics API distinguishes EXT_URL (outside website links including Google Search), YT_SEARCH (on-platform search), SHORTS (vertical swipe referral), SUBSCRIBER (homepage or subscription feature referral), NO_LINK_OTHER (unknown/direct), and ADVERTISING. These are sources of view activity, not personal subscriber states, portable customer lists, profits or algorithmic causal outcomes.
claims.limitations: Living product documentation, no owner report collected. Studio group descriptions and API codes need compatible source versioning; no public creator-level viewing, income, audience identity or referral conversion measurements.
